REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT)


 

The Government of Indonesia

Global Environment Facility Indonesia Sustainable Cities Impact Project

Grant No.: TF0B8114

Assignment Title: Transportation Project Management and Monitoring Evaluation Specialist

(National Consultant)

Reference No.: ID-TRANSPORT-BAPPENAS-556265-CS-INDV 


 

The Government of Indonesia, through the Ministry of National Development Planning/National Development  Planning  Agency  (Bappenas),  has  received  grant  funding  from  the  Global  Environment Facility (GEF) Sustainable Cities Impact Project (SCIP) through the World Bank. Part of this funding is allocated for individual consultant services.

 

The Individual consultant services are output-based and will be responsible for:

  1. Project governance and management framework. Develop management and administrative frameworks on the PIU side of the SUMP development, including setting up stakeholder relations & consultations arrangements to confirm project scope, data requirements, and monitoring methodologies have been aligned with the needs;
  2. Oversight and safeguard supervision. Manage project governance through inter-agency coordination and milestone monitoring while overseeing the contracted consulting firms to ensure data quality, deliverable integrity, and full compliance with the project ToRs and World Bank’s ESF and fiduciary requirements. This includes overseeing the administrative coordination, logistics, and documentation of Focus Group Discussions (FGDs) and steering committee meetings involving line ministries, local governments, and the World Bank;
  3. Technical advisory on urban mobility and sustainable transport planning. Provide substantive technical advisory across the SUMP development cycle, including:
  • integration  of  sustainability,  climate  resilience,  and  World  Bank  ESF  standards  into  transport planning documents;
  • review of environment, social and governance (ESG) monitoring frameworks and gender equality and social inclusion (GEDSI) to guarantee equitable engagement, transparent governance, and accountable decision-making;
  • strategic inputs for the development of Integrated Transport Authority (ITA) frameworks to support effective long-term SUMP implementation;
  • technical guidance on core transport planning methodologies, including four-step model, level of service (LOS), O/D Matrix development, concepts related to Functional Urban Area (FUA) and Transit-oriented Development (TOD), design and analysis of data collection and survey, scenario building and selection, and prioritization of programs;
  • inputs on transport economics and financing, including economic and financial appraisal of priority programs, cost-benefit and cost-effectiveness analysis, creative finance schemes (e.g. land value capture, KPBU/PPP, blended financing), and affordability and fiscal sustainability consideration.

to shape the strategic direction of the Balikpapan and Palembang SUMP, ensuring that all technical outputs align with sectoral best practices and the project’s regulatory framework.

4.   Documentation compliance and audit-readiness. Ensure that contract and project documentation is maintained complete, properly filed, and consistent with prevailing national regulations, so as to support timely contract clearance and facilitate examination by oversight bodies including the Badan Pemeriksa Keuangan (BPK). 

 

In addition, The Consultant may be required to execute following supporting activities including but not limited to:

  1. Knowledge transfer to the Directorate. Work alongside the team of Individual Consultants to strengthen the technical capabilities of the Directorate in managing complex urban mobility frameworks, transport economics and creative financing, traffic demand management, and the governance of integrated transportation systems.
  2. Support   to   World   Bank   implementation   support   missions.   Contribute   substantive   inputs   and documentation to World Bank implementation support missions, including pre-mission briefings, technical materials, and inputs to aide-memoires and management letters, ensuring that Directorate’s positions and the SUMP project’s progress are represented accurately and consistently.


 

The individual consultant services are expected to perform the service for 9 months. The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found on the following website : https://link.bappenas.go.id/TransportationME_.

 

The Directorate of Connectivity and Logistic Infrastructure at the Ministry of National Development Planning/National Development Planning Agency now invites eligible individual consultant (“Consultant”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultant should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are the relevant experience of the individual consultant in:

 

REQUIRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE

Essential Qualification

  1. Minimum requirement of a master’s degree in urban planning,  transport engineering, transport economics, transport project management, public policy, business administration, or a related field;
  2. More than 15 years of work experience in urban mobility, sustainable transport planning, and/or transport sector policy, of which at least 5 years in advisory, planning, or project management roles;
  3. Has experience in a minimum of one (1) SUMP/Pre-FS/FS project (proven by CV and supporting document(s) such as contracts, acknowledgment letter, or other related documents);
  4. Demonstrated  experience  in  project  management  and/or  monitoring  and  evaluation  of  donor- financed or government-financed transport, infrastructure, or planning projects, including managing project timelines, deliverables, and reporting cycles;
  5. Familiarity with the Indonesian national and subnational development planning system (RPJMN, RKP, RPJMD, RTRW) and relevant transport sector regulatory framework, as well as the World Bank’s Environmental and Social Framework (ESF) or equivalent safeguards systems (e.g. ADB SPS, IFC Performance Standards);
  6. Proficient in performing quantitative and qualitative data analysis in transportation sector and demonstrating strong communication and writing skills in professional English (proven by policy papers/books/studies/journals/research/essay/report/ToR sample in English) and Bahasa Indonesia;
  7. Experience working on national/international development agency operations such as Ministry of National Development Planning (Bappenas)/Ministry of Transportation/World Bank/Asian Development Bank/USAID/GIZ/GCF/KIAT, etc.

Desirable Qualifications

  1. Experience with sustainable transport, climate resilience, NDC-aligned transport interventions, or low-carbon mobility programs;
  2. Experience integrating gender equality, disability and social inclusion (GEDSI) and environment, social and governance (ESG) considerations into transport or infrastructure planning;
  3. Familiarity with the design or operationalization of metropolitan or city-level transport authorities  in Indonesia or comparable contexts;
  4. Familiarity with economic and financial appraisal of transport projects (cost-benefit and cost- effectiveness analysis) and/or transport financing mechanisms (KPBU/PPP, blended finance, land value capture, fiscal transfer schemes for Pemda);
  5. Project management certification (PMP, PRINCE2, or equivalent) and/or formal M&E training is an advantage.


 

The selected individual consultant will be based in the Jakarta (Indonesia) office.


 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s  Procurement  Regulations  for  IPF  Borrowers  July  2016,  revised  November  2017,  July  2018, November 2020, and September 2023 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

 

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Individual Consultant Selection method set out in the

Procurement Regulations.

 

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours (09.00 to 17.00 GMT+7). Interested applicant must be submit the comprehensive curriculum vitae of individual consultant before Monday, October 4, 2026  at 12.00 WIB to the following address: ulp@bappenas.go.id.

SOCIAL OFFICER (Local) - (FULL-TIME)

Preparation for Fiji Energy Transformation Project

Project Preparation Unit (PPU) | Energy Fiji Limited (EFL)
World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF)

Name of Project

Fiji Energy Transformation Project

Implementing Agency

Energy Fiji Limited (EFL)

Assignment Title

Social Officer (Local) - (Full-Time)

Organisational Unit

Project Preparation Unit (PPU)

Primary Framework

World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF)

Duty Station / Coverage

PPU office, with regular field visits across Viti Levu, Vanua Levu and Taveuni

Reporting Line

Environmental and Social (E&S) Specialist; PPU Project Manager on overall project matters

Expected Commencement

As soon as possible

Table of Contents

Table of Contents. 1

1. Introduction and Background. 3

2. Objective of the Assignment 3

3. Scope of Work. 3

3.1 Stakeholder Engagement and Community Liaison. 3

3.2 Indigenous Peoples Planning Framework (IPPF) 3

3.3 Resettlement Policy Framework (RPF) 4

3.4 Negotiated Land Agreement Due Diligence. 4

3.5 Gender and Vulnerability. 4

3.6 Labor and Working Conditions - Social Dimensions. 4

3.7 Coordination with Government Line Ministries and Agencies. 5

3.8 Capacity Building. 5

3.9 Reporting and Coordination. 5

4. Methodology and Approach. 5

5. Key Deliverables and Indicative Timing. 6

6. Assignment Duration and Work Programme. 6

7. Required Qualifications and Experience. 6

7.1 Education. 6

7.2 Professional Experience. 6

7.3 Skills and Competencies. 7

8. Reporting and Working Arrangements. 7

9. Application Requirements. 7

 

 

 

1. Introduction and Background

The Fiji Energy Transformation Project is proposed as a USD 230 million World Bank-supported initiative aimed at accelerating renewable energy, modernizing the power grid, and reforming the energy sector to attract private investment. Key interventions include large-scale solar photovoltaic (PV) and battery energy storage system (BESS) parks of 50 MW or more each, grid evacuation infrastructure, transmission line upgrades, and modernization of existing power stations across Viti Levu, Vanua Levu, and Taveuni. The project’s environmental and social risks have been classified as Substantial under the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF).

A significant portion of land in the project area is held under customary iTaukei tenure and managed through the iTaukei Land Trust Board (TLTB). Many affected communities are iTaukei Fijians who qualify as Indigenous Peoples under ESS7. The project may also involve economic and physical displacement linked to land acquisition for solar parks, transmission lines, and associated infrastructure, triggering ESS5 on Land Acquisition, Restrictions on Land Use and Involuntary Resettlement.

The Social Officer will be embedded within the PPU and will work under the day-to-day supervision of the Environmental and Social (E&S) Specialist, who has overall leadership of the project’s E&S function. The Social Officer will work in close coordination with the Environment Officer. Together, these positions constitute the project’s E&S team and are jointly responsible for delivering the suite of ESF instruments required for project appraisal and for supporting implementation thereafter.

2. Objective of the Assignment

The objective of the assignment is to support the timely preparation of all social-related ESF instruments required for appraisal, ensure ongoing and meaningful stakeholder engagement throughout project preparation and implementation, and serve as the PPU’s primary liaison with government line ministries and agencies responsible for land, indigenous affairs, and social protection.

3. Scope of Work

3.1 Stakeholder Engagement and Community Liaison

a. Lead the preparation, implementation, and updating of the project’s Stakeholder Engagement Plan (SEP), in close coordination with the E&S Specialist, who will review and finalize the instrument. The SEP must include:

  • A project-wide grievance redress mechanism (GRM), including a reporting structure for complaint escalation and resolution within specified timeframes.
  • A dedicated pathway for Sexual Exploitation and Abuse / Sexual Harassment (SEA/SH) complaints, including resolution or escalation timeframes.
  • Differentiated engagement approaches for iTaukei communities, women, and other vulnerable groups.
  • A disclosure schedule compliant with ESF requirements.

b. Serve as the PPU’s primary point of contact for community-level consultations across project sites on Viti Levu, Vanua Levu, and Taveuni. Coordinate field consultation logistics with the Environment Officer so that environmental and social consultations are sequenced and, where possible, combined to minimize the burden on communities.

c. Maintain a consultation log recording meetings, attendees disaggregated by gender and community role, issues raised, and follow-up actions. Share the log with the E&S Specialist and Environment Officer on a fortnightly basis.

d. Ensure that Free, Prior and Informed Consent (FPIC) processes are properly documented for all iTaukei communities in the project’s area of influence, in accordance with ESS7 and applicable Fijian law.

3.2 Indigenous Peoples Planning Framework (IPPF)

a. Lead the preparation of the Indigenous Peoples Planning Framework (IPPF) in accordance with ESS7. The IPPF must:

  • Liaise with the EFL Lands Team to identify all iTaukei communities and landowning units (mataqali) in the project’s area of influence.
  • Set out a methodology for social assessment and FPIC at the site-specific level.
  • Define entitlements and culturally appropriate benefit-sharing mechanisms.
  • Establish culturally sensitive grievance and feedback channels.
  • Address gender dynamics and vulnerabilities within iTaukei communities.

b. Coordinate with the E&S Specialist to ensure consistency between the IPPF, the Resettlement Policy Framework (RPF), and the SEP, so that the instruments present a coherent and non-contradictory framework for community engagement and entitlements.

c. Where site-specific Indigenous Peoples Plans (IPPs) are required, support their preparation in parallel with, or as a follow-on to, the IPPF.

3.3 Resettlement Policy Framework (RPF)

a. Support the E&S Specialist in preparing the RPF in accordance with ESS5. The Social Officer will be responsible for:

  • Conducting or supervising social baseline surveys required to inform the RPF.
  • Documenting existing land use, livelihoods, and community assets in project-affected areas.
  • Drafting the entitlement matrix in coordination with the E&S Specialist.
  • Ensuring that the RPF reflects the specificities of iTaukei land tenure and customary rights.

b. Coordinate with the Environment Officer to ensure that environmental footprint assessments underpinning the RPF, including site boundaries, buffer zones, and access routes, are accurate and consistently applied across instruments.

3.4 Negotiated Land Agreement Due Diligence

a. Support the E&S Specialist in preparing the Negotiated Land Agreement Due Diligence Report. The Social Officer will:

  • Coordinate with the EFL Lands Team and liaise with the TLTB and relevant landowning units (mataqali) to understand existing or proposed negotiated land agreements for solar park and transmission line sites.
  • Verify the voluntariness of negotiations and document indicators of undue pressure or inadequate community representation.
  • Identify gaps between existing agreements and ESF requirements and propose remediation measures.

3.5 Gender and Vulnerability

a. Integrate gender analysis into all social instruments, ensuring that the project identifies and responds to differential impacts on women, girls, and other vulnerable or marginalized groups.

b. Support the preparation of a Gender Action Plan or equivalent measures, in coordination with the E&S Specialist.

c. Identify and document vulnerable households in the project area, including elderly people, persons with disabilities, female-headed households, and households with insecure tenure, and ensure they are reflected in the RPF entitlement matrix and the IPPF.

3.6 Labor and Working Conditions - Social Dimensions

a. Contribute to the Labor Management Procedures (LMP) by preparing the social dimensions, including community hiring provisions, management of labor influx risks, SEA/SH and communicable disease risks in host communities, supply chain social due diligence requirements, and conflict resolution between workers and community members. The E&S Specialist retains overall responsibility for the LMP.

b. Coordinate with the Environment Officer on environmental health dimensions of labor influx, including waste, water, and camp management, to ensure that the LMP presents unified and internally consistent measures.

3.7 Coordination with Government Line Ministries and Agencies

The Social Officer will serve as the PPU’s primary liaison with the following entities on social matters:

  • Ministry of Lands and Mineral Resources: land acquisition procedures, state land matters, and coordination of required land surveys or valuations.
  • iTaukei Affairs Board / Ministry of iTaukei Affairs: customary governance, community protocols, and support for FPIC processes.
  • iTaukei Land Trust Board (TLTB): management of iTaukei land, negotiated agreements, lease arrangements, and consent from landowning units.
  • Department of Social Welfare / Ministry of Women, Children and Poverty Alleviation: identification of vulnerable households and gender considerations.
  • Any other relevant agency identified during preparation as having a mandate over affected communities or social protection matters.

The Social Officer will establish and maintain regular contact with focal points in each agency, keep records of correspondence and meetings, and report on ministry engagement to the E&S Specialist as part of the fortnightly joint E&S team update.

3.8 Capacity Building

a. Together with the E&S Specialist and Environment Officer, contribute to the preparation of the TOR for EFL’s institutional Environmental and Social Management System (ESMS), specifically the social management components.

b. Provide on-the-job guidance to EFL staff engaged in community liaison activities during project preparation.

3.9 Reporting and Coordination

a. Prepare monthly progress reports on social preparation activities and submit them to the E&S Specialist for integration into the consolidated E&S team report to the PPU Project Manager.

b. Maintain a live Social Risk Register tracking identified social risks and mitigation measures, updated fortnightly and shared with the E&S Specialist and Environment Officer.

c. Participate in the mandatory weekly joint E&S team meeting and the fortnightly joint risk register review.

d. Coordinate all field visits jointly with the Environment Officer and E&S Specialist. Where a visit has environmental and social dimensions, the Social Officer and Environment Officer will attend together wherever possible to minimize multiple visits and support integrated data collection.

e. Before submitting an instrument draft to the E&S Specialist, circulate it to the Environment Officer for a peer consistency check covering site boundaries, affected population figures, and mitigation commitments.

f. Support the E&S Specialist during World Bank supervision missions and technical reviews, including preparation of briefing materials and attendance at relevant meetings.

4. Methodology and Approach

The Social Officer will apply an integrated, participatory, and evidence-based approach throughout the assignment. The approach will include:

  • Desktop review of available project documents, land information, consultation records, and relevant social baseline information.
  • Field-based social assessment and community consultation across relevant project locations.
  • Culturally appropriate engagement with iTaukei communities and landowning units, including documentation of FPIC where required.
  • Coordination with the E&S Specialist, Environment Officer, EFL Lands Team, government agencies, and other relevant stakeholders.
  • Preparation, review, updating, and consistency checking of social instruments and associated records.
  • Routine monitoring through consultation logs, the Social Risk Register, progress reports, and agreed coordination meetings.

5. Key Deliverables and Indicative Timing

All deliverables are subject to World Bank review and clearance. The primary target is project appraisal. Specific submission dates will be agreed with the E&S Specialist and PPU Project Manager upon commencement.

6. Assignment Duration and Work Programme

The position is expected to commence as soon as possible and will cover the full project preparation period through appraisal, with the possibility of extension into implementation. Upon commencement, the Social Officer will agree detailed submission dates, priorities, and an activity schedule with the E&S Specialist and PPU Project Manager. Regular field travel will be required.

7. Required Qualifications and Experience

7.1 Education

  • A university degree in social sciences, anthropology, development studies, law, or a related field. A postgraduate degree is an advantage.

7.2 Professional Experience

  • A minimum of five (5) years of relevant professional experience in social safeguards or social risk management on infrastructure or energy projects.
  • Demonstrated experience with World Bank ESF instruments, including ESS1, ESS2, ESS5, ESS7 and ESS10, or equivalent IFC Performance Standards.
  • Demonstrated experience working with Indigenous Peoples and customary land tenure systems in the Pacific or comparable contexts.
  • Experience liaising with government land administration agencies. Familiarity with Fiji’s iTaukei land tenure system and the role of the TLTB is a strong advantage.

7.3 Skills and Competencies

  • Strong facilitation and consultation skills, including experience conducting consultations with rural and indigenous communities.
  • Strong coordination, record-keeping, analytical, and report-writing skills.
  • Ability to work collaboratively within a multidisciplinary E&S and project preparation team.
  • Excellent written and spoken English. Knowledge of iTaukei Fijian or Fiji Hindi is an advantage.

8. Reporting and Working Arrangements

The Social Officer is a full-time position based at the PPU office, with regular field visits to project sites across Viti Levu, Vanua Levu, and Taveuni. The Social Officer reports to the E&S Specialist on a day-to-day basis and to the PPU Project Manager on overall project matters. The Social Officer will participate in the weekly joint E&S team meeting and the broader PPU team meeting.

9. Application Requirements

Interested candidates should submit a curriculum vitae and a cover letter describing their relevant experience in relation to the scope of work set out in this TOR. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis.

 

Submission

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia

Ministry of Irrigation and Lowlands

Project: Climate Resilient Irrigation for Sustainable Production (CRISP)

Credit No.: IDA-P182114

Assignment Title: Consultancy services for the feasibility study, detailed design, tender document preparation, construction supervision, & contract administration for the Gidabo Left Bank New Irrigation Development project, an area of 5,000ha for the Feasibility Study and 1,000ha for the Detailed Design

Procurement Reference No.: ET-MOIL-544259-CS-QCBS

The Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Climate Resilient Irrigation for Sustainable Production (CRISP) Project. The implementing agency, the Ministry of Irrigation and Lowlands, intends to apply part of the proceeds for the consulting service.

The consulting service (‘the service’) includes conducting the feasibility study, detailed design, tender document preparation, construction supervision, & contract administration for the Gidabo Left Bank New Irrigation Development project, an area of 5,000ha for the Feasibility Study and 1,000ha for the Detailed Design.

The Objective of the Assignment: The objectives of this consultancy service shall include the following major categories, but not limited to:

      1. Conduct Feasibility Study
      2. Prepare detail design
      3. Prepare tender Document
      4. Provide Contract Administration and Construction Supervision for the Gidabo Left Bank Irrigation Scheme.

Scope of the service: The scope of the consultancy services comprises, but is not limited to:

  1. Several basin-wide and scheme-specific studies have been conducted for the Rift Valley basin and Gidabo- left bank, as well as the bigger Gidabo (including Gidabo right bank). The consultant will make use of this information/data from all available sources through desk-work, combined with the initial two days of field visits and beneficiary consultation meetings at the Gidabo irrigation scheme, which will serve as a base to prepare the Inception Report.
  2. Conduct feasibilitylevel field surveys, investigations, and explorations for 5,000 ha of the Gidabo irrigation scheme on the Oromia side. This area comprises new, previously undeveloped (virgin) land that requires pumping due to elevation differences. It is located on the left bank of the already-constructed, concrete-lined main canal, which will also be investigated by the consultant.
  3. Carry out technical, economic/financial, social, and environmental analysis, among others, to come up with clear recommendations for the optimal crop and irrigation and drainage technology options selection and prepare a complete set of feasibility report to irrigate 5,000 ha.
  4. Once MILLs validate the feasibility study report, see Section 7 schedule of reporting, undertake detailed design level surveys and technical investigations (as detailed in Section 7) for 1,000ha with a focus on the feasibility level selected irrigation and drainage technology option. This includes determining optimal pump intake location and investigating improvement needs (including safety) of the main canal upstream of the intake. 
  5. Given that the development of a number of irrigation schemes benefiting from the same dam and main canal is planned or progressing, the assignment includes assessing their implication and ensuring water availability in all circumstances.
  6. Prepare detailed design, engineering drawings, and bid document to irrigate 1,000ha as well as the improvements needed along the above-mentioned main canal. This includes specifying pump capacities and power requirements, optimal energy source, as well as specifying/quantifying irrigation equipment, locating sources of construction materials, proposing construction/installation method, and preparing engineering cost estimates (including O&M costs).
  7. Undertake contract management and construction supervision of 1,000ha modernized irrigation and drainage infrastructures, as well as drafting the operation and maintenance manual during the detailed design stage (to be finalized at the end of supervision to include, among others, the as-built drawings). 
  8. Assess the institutional and O&M capacity of Oromia Irrigation and Pastoralist Development Bureau (OIPDB) and the water user groups, recommend the capacity building needs, and provide them with the required support to effectively and efficiently undertake their respective O&M roles. In case a pressurized water application is to be recommended, the consultant is required to prepare the Terms of Reference (based on its feasibility level draft design) for the competent company to design, build/install, and operate for two years while building the operational capacity of OIPDB and the water users’ groups.

Service Duration; The total duration of the service is 9 months (270 calendar days) for the feasibility study and detailed design and tender documents, and 18 months (540 calendar days) for Construction supervision and Contract Administration.

The Ministry of Irrigation and Lowlands now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The short-listing criteria are: Core business and years in business, qualifications and experience in the field of assignment, organizational, managerial and technical capabilities of the firm.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.13, 3.15 and 3.16 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers Procurement in Investment Project Financing Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services, Seventh Edition September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. 

Consultants may associate with other firms in the form of a joint venture or a sub-consultancy to enhance their qualifications. But should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality and Cost Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the procurement regulation.

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours 9:00 a.m. to 12:00 noon and 2:00 pm to 4:30 p.m. from Monday to Friday. Consultants may get the soft copy of the ToR upon sending written request to the email address: huscrisp26@gmail.com.

Expressions of interest must be delivered in written form to the address below in person on or before 5th October 2026, 4:30 P.M

The Address

The Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia, Ministry of Irrigation and Lowlands, 4th Floor, Attn: Ato Daba Jinfesa Shanko, Engineering Procurement Lead Executive Street Address: Kazanchis Business District, Kirkos sub-city 17/18, City: Addis Ababa, Country: Ethiopia Tel: (251) 118 552 665/66, E-mail: Dabajshanko@gmail.com/swakgari12@gmail.com

pendientes.Oportunidad: Website for Green Plan
pendientes.Texto:
1. The Republic of Lebanon (The Borrower) represented by the Council for Development and Reconstruction (CDR) has received a loan from the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (World Bank) in the amount of US$ 200 million for the Green, Agri-food Transformation for Economic Recovery Project (GATE) – N°: 9576-LB

The Council for Development and Reconstruction (CDR), has delegated the implementation and management of sub-component 2.1 of the Project to the Green Plan (GP). The GP intends to apply part of the proceeds of this loan for eligible payments for the consultancy services to be procured under the project.

The consulting services comprise the development of a website for the Green Plan.

 

2. Objective of the assignment

The objective of this assignment is to design, develop, and deploy a secure, scalable, and user-friendly website that:

® Promotes Green Plan programs and activities and Gate Project activities

® Serves as the official communication platform for the Green Plan, including the webpage development of GATE Project;

® Ensures public access to project information, progress reports, …

® Enhances stakeholder engagement and communication by providing access to project information, updates, and communication channels.

® Facilitates grievance management by enabling stakeholders to submit grievances through a dedicated Grievance Redress Mechanism (GRM);

® Enables efficient internal content management by non-technical staff.

 

3. Scope of Services

The Consultant shall provide all services required for the successful implementation of the assignment, including but not limited to: requirements analysis, system design, UX/UI design, prototyping, system development, CMS implementation, configuration of functional modules, integration of dashboards, GIS and external systems, testing and quality assurance, deployment and go-live support, training and capacity building, warranty, maintenance, technical support, and preparation of all documentation and handover materials required for final acceptance.

The assignment shall be implemented in the following phases:

- Phase I: Requirements Analysis and System Design

- Phase II: System Development and Configuration

- Phase III: Testing, Deployment, and Go-Live

- Phase IV: Training and Capacity Building

- Phase V: Warranty, Maintenance, and Technical Support

These phases describe the implementation sequence only and shall not be interpreted as payment milestones.

 

4. Invitation for Expressions of Interest

The Green Plan now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. Consultant brochures may also be included in the Expression of Interest (EOI).

 

5. Evaluation Criteria

Expressions of Interest will be evaluated using a 100-point scoring system based on the following criteria and weights:

Criterion 1: General experience of the firm (30/100)

This criterion assesses the firm’s overall experience and track record, including years of relevant experience and the number and type of websites successfully delivered.  Criterion 2: Experience in Similar Assignments within the last 10 years (25/100)

This criterion assesses the firm's experience in successfully delivering assignments of similar nature, scope and complexity to the required services. Similar assignments may include, but are not limited to, website design and development, CMS implementation and customization, online forms, interactive website functionalities, and website maintenance and technical support.

The Firm shall provide details of its own similar contracts, including, for each reference project, the client's name, project title, a brief description of the services provided, website URL(s) (where applicable), CMS/platform used, completion date, and contract value.

- Criterion 3: Qualifications and Experience of Key Experts (25/100)

The proposed scoring under this criterion would be:

1. Team Leader (Key Expert) (15/25)

- University degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Software Engineering, or a related field.

- Minimum 7 years of professional experience in website design, development, and implementation.

- Minimum 5 years of professional experience in managing and delivering similar website development assignments, including CMS-based and multilingual websites.

2. Website Designer (Key Expert) (10/25)

- University degree or equivalent qualification in Web Design, Graphic Design, Computer Science, or a related field.

- Minimum 7 years of professional experience in designing user-friendly and responsive websites.

- Minimum 5 years of professional experience in designing modern website interfaces, including multilingual and mobile-friendly websites.

Alternatively, the REOI evaluation could remain limited to the consulting firm's experience and capacity, with information on available technical resources provided only for reference, as currently reflected in the REOI.

Criterion 4: Experience with Government Institutions, Donor-Funded Projects and NGOs within the last 10 years (20/100)

This criterion assesses the firm's experience in providing similar services to government institutions, donor-funded projects, international organizations, and non-governmental organizations (NGOs). It evaluates the firm's familiarity with the working environment, requirements and standards typically associated with such organizations.

The firm shall provide relevant portfolios and supporting documents to substantiate the information provided under the above evaluation criteria. Such documents may include, where applicable, website links, project references, completion certificates, client references, or other evidence demonstrating the Applicant’s experience and qualifications.

The Expression of Interest should not exceed 50 pages.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.13, 3.15, and 3.16 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” (February 2025), which set forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but should clearly indicate whether the association is in the form of a joint venture or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract if selected.

The selection will be conducted using the Consultant’s Qualification-Based Selection (CQS) method in accordance with the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (November 2020).

Further information may be obtained in writing during office hours, from 08:30–15:00 (Beirut local time) by email at procurement.gp.gate@gmail.com.

Expressions of Interest must be submitted electronically to: procurement.gp.gate@gmail.com

Deadline for submission: Monday, 5 October 2026 at 12:00 noon (Beirut local time).

Lebanese Republic

Council for Development and Reconstruction (CDR)

GREEN, AGRI-FOOD TRANSFORMATION FOR ECONOMIC RECOVERY (GATE)

The CDR intends to apply a portion of the proceeds of this loan to eligible payments under a consulting services contract for the “Detailed Designs, Tender Documents and Supervision for the Construction of Sludge Solar Dryers for Zahlé and Charqiyeh Wastewater Treatment Plants (GC2C2c)”.

The full Terms of References (TOR) version can be found on CDR website www.cdr.gov.lb, click on the Procurement tag for more info.

The Main objective of this assignment is to reduce the volume and moisture content of the sludge generated at the wastewater treatment plants, thereby improving sludge handling and management with the intention to improve pollution management and to generate potential agricultural benefits for surrounding agricultural activities.

The Consultant shall provide the Employer the following main services (Tasks) and documents (all details about each task are provided in the TOR):

  • List of ONLY relevant similar projects (maximum 10 projects) as defined in the Terms of References, ongoing and/or completed within the last 10 years, indicating the provided services, the percentage of participation in JV (if any), and the size/value of relevant contracts (in USD and in person-month).

Only projects completed within the last ten (10) years shall be considered.
  • Overall firm's employees list and personnel availability and structure (list, number, organization structure, etc… of the core, backstopping and supporting staff).
  • Experience in Lebanon and/or the Middle East.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.13, 3.15 and 3.16 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, Sixth Edition, February 2025”, which set forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

Consultants may associate with another firm in the form of a "Joint Venture" to enhance their qualifications, name and nationality of the partner in charge shall be specified. A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality and Cost Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations. Eligible firms, which have submitted the necessary statements in a satisfactory responsive way, might be short listed.

 

The shortlisting criteria for firms interested in providing these services include:

Key experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours (from 09:00 to 14:00 Beirut local Time).

pendientes.Texto:
LEBANESE REPUBLIC

MINISTRY OF FINANCE

Lebanon Fiscal Management Project - Project Coordination Unit

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES - FIRMS SELECTION)

Country

Lebanese Republic

Project

Lebanon Fiscal Management Project (FMP) (P181155)

Loan No.

IBRD-96440

Assignment Title

Consulting Firm for IFMIS Implementation Support

Reference No. (as per Procurement Plan)

LB-MOF-568525-CS-QCBS

Market Approach

Open - International

Deadline for Submission of Expressions of Interest

5 October 2026 at 15:00, Beirut local time

 

  1. Financing

The Lebanese Republic has received financing from the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD) toward the cost of the Lebanon Fiscal Management Project (FMP), and intends to apply part of the proceeds of this financing to eligible payments under the contract for the consulting services described below.

The consulting services (“the Services”) will be provided to the Ministry of Finance of the Lebanese Republic (“the Client”), which is the implementing agency for the Project.

  1. Objective and scope of the Services

The objective of the assignment is to support the Ministry of Finance (MoF) in the successful preparation, procurement, implementation, and institutionalization of a fit-for-purpose Integrated Financial Management Information System (IFMIS) that strengthens public financial management, improves fiscal transparency and accountability, and supports the Government of Lebanon’s reform agenda.

The selected consulting firm will serve as an independent technical advisor and implementation oversight consultant. The Firm will not be responsible for supplying, configuring, implementing, or deploying the IFMIS solution, which will be procured separately through a competitive process.

The Services will include, inter alia:

  • Supporting IFMIS governance, project operationalization, project management, risk management, and quality assurance arrangements;
  • Reviewing the legal and regulatory framework relevant to digital public financial management and recommending required reforms;
  • Undertaking Business Process Reengineering (BPR) and defining future “to-be” processes, roles, responsibilities, workflow hierarchies, user requirements, and internal controls;
  • Preparing the Functional Requirements Specification (FRS) and System Requirements Specification (SRS), including integration, cybersecurity, data protection, business continuity, and reporting requirements;
  • Assessing data readiness and preparing the data migration strategy and plan;
  • Supporting key PFM enablers, including the Treasury Single Account (TSA) and reform of the Budget Classification and Chart of Accounts (BC-CoA);
  • Preparing the IFMIS acquisition roadmap, PPSD, Early Market Engagement activities, and the complete Request for Proposals (RFP), and providing technical support during the procurement process; and
  • Providing independent technical oversight and quality assurance during IFMIS implementation, including configuration review, data migration, UAT/OAT, training, go-live, stabilization, and sustainability planning.

Cross-cutting activities will include change management, enterprise risk management, cybersecurity and data protection, capacity building, and knowledge transfer throughout the assignment.

  1. Duration, place of performance, and contract type

The assignment will comprise two components:

  • Part A: Lump-Sum Component (Phases A–E): expected to be completed within approximately twelve (12) months from contract commencement, covering the preparatory, analytical, requirements-definition, and procurement-support activities.
  • Part B: Time-Based Component (Phase F): expected to extend for up to twenty-four (24) months, commencing upon effectiveness of the IFMIS vendor contract and written authorization by the MoF. The actual duration and level of effort will be aligned with the IFMIS vendor’s implementation schedule and the project closing date.

The Services are expected to be performed through a combination of in-country engagements at the Ministry of Finance in Beirut, Lebanon, and remote inputs, as appropriate to the nature and requirements of each phase. The required level and timing of expert mobilization, particularly during Phase F, will be agreed with and authorized by the MoF.

The contract will therefore comprise a Lump-Sum component for Phases A–E and a Time-Based component for Phase F.

  1. Terms of Reference

The detailed Terms of Reference for the assignment is attached to this Request for Expressions of Interest. It may also be obtained at the address given in paragraph 10 below, or requested by email.

  1. Invitation

The Ministry of Finance now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consulting firms should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

Expressions of interest shall be structured so as to address each of the shortlisting criteria set out in paragraph 6 below, in the order in which they appear. Submissions that do not address these criteria may not be considered.

  1. Shortlisting criteria

The consultant will be shortlisted on the basis of the following criteria. Only the qualifications and experience of the firm - and, where an association is proposed, of its joint venture partners - will be assessed at this stage.

  1. Core business and proven corporate experience in IFMIS advisory, public financial management reform, IFMIS procurement support, implementation oversight, or closely related public-sector digital transformation assignments.
  2. Demonstrated experience in IFMIS advisory, procurement preparation, and/or implementation support in at least three countries during the last ten (10) years.
  3. Demonstrated experience in business process reengineering and definition of functional and technical requirements for large-scale public financial management information systems, including preparation of FRS/SRS, data migration requirements, and system integration specifications.
  4. Experience preparing procurement strategies and RFP packages for complex COTS-based government information systems, and providing technical advisory support during evaluation, contract negotiations, implementation oversight, testing, go-live and stabilization.
  5. Proven experience working in fragile, conflict-affected or post-crisis environments. Experience in the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region and experience under World Bank-financed or other multilateral development bank-financed projects will be considered an advantage.
  6. Demonstrated managerial and organizational capacity to mobilize and coordinate a multidisciplinary team covering IFMIS, PFM, business process reengineering, budget classification/chart of accounts, treasury/TSA, legal reform, ICT procurement, data migration, change management and independent quality assurance.

Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers”, Seventh Edition, September 2025 (“the Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. The Procurement Regulations are available on the World Bank’s website at www.worldbank.org/procurement.

  1. Associations

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, but shall indicate clearly whether the association takes the form of a joint venture or of a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all partners shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract if selected.

  1. Selection method and shortlist

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality- and Cost-Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

The shortlist will contain not fewer than five (5) and not more than eight (8) firms. Only shortlisted Consultants will be invited to submit proposals, and will be notified in writing.

  1. Submission of expressions of interest

Expressions of interest must be delivered in written form, in English, to the address given in paragraph 12 below (in person, by mail, or by e-mail) no later than 5 October 2026 at 15:00 hours, Beirut local time.

  • Submissions sent by e-mail shall be in a format that cannot be altered (PDF preferred), shall not exceed 10 MB per message, and shall bear the following subject line: “EOI – IFMIS  Consulting Firm - LB-MOF-568525-CS-QCBS - [name of firm]”.
  • The Ministry of Finance will acknowledge receipt of each expression of interest by return e-mail. A Consultant that has not received an acknowledgement within one (1) working day of submission should contact the Ministry at the address given below.
  • Expressions of interest should not exceed twenty-five (25) pages, excluding the covering letter.
  1. Address for information and submission

Further information may be obtained at the address below during office hours, 08:00 to 16:00 hours Beirut local time, Monday to Friday:

Amer Syagha / Procurement Specialist

Project Coordination Unit - Lebanon Fiscal Management Project

Ministry of Finance - The Republic of Lebanon

Riad El Solh

Beirut, Lebanon

E-mail: amers@finance.gov.lb

Website: www.finance.gov.lb

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION

 

Country: ALBANIA

Name of the Project: Clean and Resilient Environment for Blue Sea (Care4BlueSea)

IBRD Loan No.: 95070-AL

Project ID Number: P176163

Assignment Title: Technical Assistance to support the implementation of Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR)

Reference No.: AL-MTE-573446-CS-CQS

 

The Ministry of Environment has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Care4BlueSea initiative and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The consulting services (“the Services”) include provision of support the Ministry of Environment in the practical operationalization of circular economic instruments, primarily through structured capacity-building modules, workshops, and international knowledge exchange, focusing on:

  • Establishment and operationalization of Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) systems
  • Development of circular economic approaches and sector-specific applications (e.g., packaging, tourism, resource efficiency)
  • Strengthening institutional capacity through hands-on, practice-oriented learning

The assignment should prioritize transfer of operational know-how, practical system design, and stakeholder alignment rather than standalone analytical outputs. The Implementation Period is up to 12 months from commencement date.

The Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found in the link below: https://mjedisi.gov.al/newsroom/kerkese-per-shprehje-interesi-3/

The Ministry of Environment now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

The Consultants shall fulfill the following minimum requirements:

The Consultant shall be a legally registered firm, joint venture or consortium with substantial practical and operational experience in waste management, recycling, Extended Producer Responsibility and circular economy. The qualifications shall demonstrate that the Consultant has the institutional capacity and first-hand operational knowledge required to deliver a practice-oriented assignment of this nature.

The Consultant should demonstrate:

  • At least five (5) years of corporate or professional experience in waste management, recycling, resource management, circular economy or closely related sectors.
  • Demonstrated direct experience in the design, establishment, implementation and/or operation of EPR or Producer Responsibility Organization (PRO) systems for packaging waste, preferably in one or more EU Member States.
  • Practical experience across relevant parts of the packaging and recycling value chain, including producer or retail interfaces, collection, sorting, recycling, secondary-material management and operational compliance with recycling targets.
  • Demonstrated experience with circular economy business models and resource-efficiency approaches, including design for recycling, closed-loop solutions, material-flow optimization and/or deposit-return systems.
  • Sound familiarity with the EU regulatory environment for packaging, EPR and circular economy, and experience translating regulatory requirements into operational processes and business arrangements.
  • Capacity to mobilize senior operational specialists and to provide practical exposure to functioning EPR, sorting, recycling, retail or circular economy systems through workshops, case-based learning and operational examples.

The shortlisting criteria are:

  • Core business and years in business – 30 points
  • Past experience in similar assignments – 60 points
  • Availability of qualified staff among the firm to perform the assignment – 10 points

Key Experts will not be evaluated at this stage.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” September 2023 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Consultant’s Qualifications based Selection (CQS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours 09.00-16:00 from Monday to Thursday and 09.00-13.00 Friday.

Expressions of interest must be delivered in a written form to the address below (in person, or by mail, or by e-mail) by October 5, 2026.

 

Protocol Office

Clean and Resilient Environment for Blue Sea Project

Attn: Mr. Elton Nino, Project Manager

Ministry of Environment 

Address: Blv. “Dëshmorët e Kombit”, No. 1, Tirana, Albania

E-mail: elton_nino@live.com
