Noumea, New Caledonia, 29/09/2026

 

Statistical Innovation and Capacity Building in the Pacific Islands (PACSTAT)

 

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES)

 

GRANT NUMBER E633-P3, P168182

Assignment Title: Regional OpenCRVS Technical Support Services for Pacific Countries

Reference No.: FJ-SPC-572068-CS-CQS / REOI26-10665

 

The Pacific Community (www.spc.int) has received financing in the amount of USD 6.0 million equivalent from the World Bank toward the cost of the Statistical Innovation and Capacity Building in the Pacific Islands Project, and it intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

SPC now invites eligible consulting firms to express their interest in providing consultancy services for the assignment entitled “Regional OpenCRVS Technical Support Services for Pacific Countries”.

The assignment is expected to start in December 2026 for an initial period of 3 months, followed by ongoing annual services, subject to funding. The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) are available with this Request for Expressions of Interest. Interested consulting firms should submit information demonstrating their qualifications and relevant experience.

The consulting firm will be selected using the Consultant Qualifications Selection (CQS) method, in accordance with the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers:

  • Stage 1: Expressions of Interest submitted will be evaluated against the required experience and minimum qualification requirements set out in section 8.0 of the Terms of Reference.
  • Stage 2: The firm ranked highest from the EOI evaluation will be invited to submit a combined technical and financial proposal under an RFP process.

The attention of interested consulting firms is drawn to paragraphs 3.13, 3.15, and 3.16 of the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (Seventh Edition, September 2025) (“the Regulations”), which set out the World Bank’s policy on Conflict of Interest applicable to consulting services:

The World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers – Seventh Edition, September 2025

Further information can be obtained at the address below by e-mail.

Expressions of interest must be delivered in a written form to the address below by e-mail no later than 13/10/2026 by 23:45 Noumea Time (GMT+11).

 

Att: SPC Procurement Unit

email: procurement@spc.int

Reference: FJ-SPC-572068-CS-CQS-REOI26-10665

 

 

 

TERMS OF REFERENCE

FIRM / CONSULTING SERVICES

Regional OpenCRVS Technical Support Services (Pacific CRVS Programme)

Assignment Title:

Regional OpenCRVS Technical Support Services for Pacific Countries

Location

Remote, with virtual engagement with SPC and participating Pacific countries

Planned Duration

Initial period 1 December 2026 to 28 February 2027, followed by an annual service from 1 March 2027, subject to funding

Expected Starting Date

1 December 2026

Reference No

FJ-SPC-572068-CS-CQS / REOI26-10665

1.0 Background:

The Pacific Community (SPC) has received financing from the World Bank under the Statistical Innovation and Capacity Building in the Pacific Islands Project (PacStat) to support strengthened statistical systems and related data services in the Pacific. This assignment will be financed under PacStat Phase 1 Additional Financing and is expected to be completed by February 2027.

SPC’s Statistics for Development Division supports Pacific Island Countries and Territories to strengthen official statistics, including the availability and use of administrative and demographic data for evidence-based planning, policy and reporting. Civil Registration and Vital Statistics (CRVS) systems are an important part of this work, as they record vital events such as births, deaths, marriages, divorces and adoptions and generate data for planning, monitoring and decision-making.

OpenCRVS is an open-source digital public good designed to support civil registration in low-resource settings. SPC, with funding from Bloomberg Philanthropies, has been working with OpenCRVS and Pacific countries to strengthen digital CRVS systems, with implementation or planned deployment in countries including Niue, Cook Islands, Tonga, Tuvalu and Kiribati. SPC also operates a regional Mortality Coding Portal built on the same platform.

A review of OpenCRVS support options has identified the need for a sustainable regional technical support arrangement. Current arrangements differ across countries, including hosting environments, infrastructure providers, configuration partners and support practices. The approach adopted is a single regional provider contracted to SPC to deliver combined Level 2 technical support and Level 3 expert technical support across participating configurations. Participating countries retain self-service and first-contact support. SPC retains coordination, contract management and service oversight. OpenCRVS provides core platform support, which is funded by OpenCRVS and is not part of this assignment.

The assignment covers up to six configurations: five participating countries and the SPC Mortality Coding Portal. An extension beyond the end of February 2027 is subject to a funding proposal to Bloomberg Philanthropies. The funding is expected to be confirmed at the end of 2026.

2.0 Objective of the assignment

To provide a regional OpenCRVS technical support arrangement for participating Pacific countries and the SPC Mortality Coding Portal, so that these systems remain available, secure, supported on current software versions and operable by the registration offices that depend on them.

The provider will deliver combined Level 2 and Level 3 support, take responsibility for version currency and security patching, operate the ticketing and knowledge management function through which the service runs, and work with country first-contact support and with SPC to maintain a consistent standard of service across all configurations.

Any support arrangement beyond 28 February 2027, including a possible extension or follow-on contract, would be subject to confirmation of future funding, satisfactory performance, and participating country requirements.

3.0 Scope of Services

The provider will deliver regional OpenCRVS technical support focused on combined Level 2 technical support and Level 3 expert technical support. Country-level self-service and first-contact support remains with participating countries. SPC provides regional coordination, contract and relationship management, and service oversight. The provider operates the ticketing and knowledge management function; the records it holds are owned by the participating countries.

The support levels are defined as follows:

Level

Description

Typical work

Sits with

L0

Self-service

• Guides, FAQs and quick-reference materials

• Multi-tenant knowledge base, reflecting each country’s own configuration

• Receiving and logging queries through the channels users actually use

• Password resets and account unlocks

• User administration — creating, amending and deactivating accounts

• Access approvals by the National System Admin, with named backup cover

• Distinguishing user error from system fault

• "How do I" guidance and reinforcement of training

• Escalating to L2 with enough detail to act on

OpenCRVS

 

The following table outlines details of what is to be delivered for combined Level 2 technical support and Level 3 expert technical support:

Scope area

Provider responsibilities

Key outputs

Mobilisation and transition

Receive configuration handover for each participating configuration; produce and agree a baseline record for each; agree and implement access arrangements including break-glass provision; stand up ticketing and knowledge base; install monitoring and alerting; brief country first-contact personnel. Time-boxed and completed within the initial period.

Baseline records signed off by incumbent and provider; access schedules; ticketing and knowledge base live; monitoring live; transition completion report.

Incident management

Receive, classify, triage, investigate and resolve incidents escalated from country first-contact support and from monitoring, against the service levels at Section 5.0. Manage major incidents and communicate status to SPC and affected countries.

Resolved incidents, ticket records, major incident reports, monthly service-level performance reporting.

Problem management

Identify recurring incidents and underlying causes; propagate preventive fixes across configurations where the same cause is present; maintain known-error records.

Root cause records, known-error register, preventive actions applied and recorded.

Releases, upgrades and patching

Plan and deliver upgrades twice yearly across all configurations, including configuration work, regression testing, user acceptance support, deployment and rollback planning. Apply security patches out of cycle without waiting for the next scheduled upgrade. Apply hotfixes where relevant to a configuration, subject to smoke testing rather than full acceptance testing.

Release plans and records, upgrade completion reports, patch records, version state register.

Version currency

Maintain every configuration on a version supported by OpenCRVS throughout the contractual arrangement. Report version state for every configuration at each service review. Common version alignment across configurations is not required.

Version state register, upgrade schedule, exception reporting where a configuration is at risk.

Preventive maintenance and monitoring

Operate monitoring and alerting across all production configurations with alerts acknowledged within the support window; verify backups monthly for each configuration; complete a documented restore test for each configuration twice yearly; perform certificate, dependency and log checks.

Monitoring records, backup verification records, restore test reports, maintenance notes.

Ticketing and knowledge management

Operate a multi-tenant ticketing system and knowledge base with a regional view and a separate view for each configuration; maintain troubleshooting notes, procedures and configuration documentation. 3.1 Outside scope

The day rates are held to give countries a ready and pre-competed route, not to confer exclusivity on the provider.

  • End-user devices, local networks and connectivity.
  • Delivery of end-user training, and new country implementations or data migration.
  • Civil registration business analysis and regulatory advisory services.
  • Level 4 core platform support, which is provided by OpenCRVS at its own cost and is not to be priced by bidders. See Section 5.3.

5.3 Matters outside the provider’s control and core defect exemption

Service levels apply to matters within the provider’s control. This includes configuration faults, access and permission problems, integration failures, release and upgrade activity, and the escalation and pursuit of infrastructure faults with the responsible party.

Level 4 core platform support is provided by OpenCRVS, funded by OpenCRVS, and made available on equal terms to any provider appointed under this assignment. Requests are raised through the published OpenCRVS route and are triaged on priority alongside requests from all other implementations. It is offered as a service level objective and not as a contractual commitment. Bidders must not include any charge for Level 4 support and must not assume preferential access to it.

Where investigation establishes that the root cause of an incident is a defect in the OpenCRVS core product, the provider’s resolution clock stops from the point at which the core defect is established and the request is raised. The evidence establishing the core defect must be recorded in the ticket. The provider’s obligation resumes when a fix or hotfix is made available, and the provider is required to apply it promptly to affected configurations, subject to smoke testing.

Faults relating to country infrastructure, power, connectivity, local devices, external systems or country-controlled decisions are similarly outside the provider’s control and are managed through agreed escalation, with the provider responsible for pursuit and communication rather than for resolution.

5.4 Service credits and persistent failure

Service credits are assessed quarterly against the quarterly charge and are earned on the proportion of critical and high severity targets met in the quarter, counting response and resolution targets together.

In addition, each of the following carries a credit of five per cent of the quarterly charge in its own right:

  • a security patch not applied within the period agreed for it;
  • a scheduled restore test not completed within the quarter in which it falls;
  • a scheduled upgrade cycle not delivered within the agreed window;
  • any shift within the support window left unstaffed.

Credits from all sources aggregate and are capped at fifteen per cent of the quarterly charge in any quarter. Credits are not applied where the cause falls under Section 5.3, nor where delay results from a participating country declining or deferring an upgrade window, access approval or other decision within its control.

Where the credit threshold at the fifteen per cent level is reached in two consecutive quarters, or where any of the four failures listed above occurs in two consecutive quarters, SPC may terminate the contract on thirty days’ written notice without cause and without liability for early termination charges. This provision exists because a capped credit regime alone is not a sufficient incentive on a contract of this size, and because the material remedy for sustained underperformance is exit rather than rebate.

During the initial period, service credits apply to critical incident response only. All other measures are reported but not scored until the annual service commences. The persistent failure provision above applies from the commencement of the annual service.

6.0 Reporting Requirements

The provider reports to the Programme Lead CRVS or designated SPC focal point. Reporting must be clear, concise and evidence-based, and must support contract oversight, service-level monitoring and risk management.

  • Monthly support report covering incidents, service-level performance, open issues, escalations, risks, security and access matters, version state and planned activities.

  • Immediate notification to SPC and the affected country of any critical incident, suspected security incident, unauthorised access concern or major service disruption.
  • A quarterly service review pack, and attendance at the service review, covering all configurations together.
  • An end-of-period performance and transition report at the end of each contract period.

7.0 Working Arrangements

This is a remote assignment. No travel is anticipated unless separately agreed in writing by SPC. The provider must be able to work effectively across Pacific time zones and within the support window at Section 5.1.

7.1 Roles

Participating countries provide self-service and first-contact support. Each country nominates a first-contact role holder, who may be a registration officer or an information technology officer as the country prefers. The role is to be reachable during the country’s working day, to attempt documented first-contact steps, and to raise tickets to the agreed template and standard. SPC will secure these commitments through its agreement with each participating country.

SPC coordinates country relationships, holds the contract, chairs the quarterly service review and approves the annual workplan. SPC does not operate a technical support tier.

The provider delivers combined Level 2 and Level 3 support as set out at Section 3.0 and provides first-contact support for the Mortality Coding Portal.

7.2 Access and break-glass provision

Country-approved access arrangements must be agreed for each configuration before service commencement, covering remote access requirements, approval pathways, access logging, monitoring, suspension and revocation.

In addition, the provider must hold break-glass access to each configuration, enabling it to act where first-contact support is unavailable or unable to perform a required action. Break-glass provision comprises accounts at registrar and national system administrator level, and secure shell access where required. Use is subject to country approval, is recorded in the product audit trail, and generates logged alerts. Bidders should price on the basis that this provision will be in place.

7.3 Data protection and data minimisation

Civil registration personal data must not be entered into ticket bodies, attachments, knowledge base articles or reporting. Incidents must reference records by identifier, and investigation requiring access to record content must take place within the country’s own environment.

Where a request is raised to OpenCRVS core support, personal data must be removed or obscured from any log extract, screenshot or screen recording before submission, as core support requests are handled through a public channel.

Ticket records, knowledge base content and reporting are owned by the participating countries. The provider must be able to export them in full, in a documented and reusable format, at any time on request and on expiry or termination of the contract.

7.4 Backup, retention and recovery

Backup arrangements comprise two layers, held by different parties.

The application backup is automated within the OpenCRVS deployment. The provider is responsible for ensuring that it is configured and operating for every configuration, that the staging environment is restoring from it on a daily basis, and that retention is set to a value agreed with the country. A minimum retention of thirty days applies. Where a configuration is found on a shorter retention, the provider must raise this with the country and SPC and implement the agreed value.

An off-site or separate-region copy of each configuration’s data must exist. Provision and retention of that copy sits with the participating country and its infrastructure provider and is outside the provider’s scope. The provider is responsible for confirming at baseline that the arrangement exists, recording its frequency and retention, reporting its status at each service review, and escalating to SPC and the country where it is absent or has lapsed.

The provider must verify backups monthly for each configuration and complete a documented restore test for each configuration twice yearly. Verification means confirming that the backup has run, is complete and is within retention; restore testing means demonstrating that data can in fact be recovered from it.

Bidders should note that participating configurations are not currently on OpenCRVS 2.1 or later, in which a deployment will not start unless its backup service is operating. On earlier versions a backup failure does not announce itself. The baseline record required at Section 4.0 must therefore establish, for each configuration, whether an automated backup is configured and running, the retention set, whether a daily staging restore is in place, and what off-site arrangement exists. These are to be treated as matters to be established rather than confirmed.

Backup failure, whether of the application backup or of the off-site arrangement, must be notified to SPC and the affected country immediately in accordance with Section 6.0.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

The Guangdong Administration for Market Regulation has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the China Food Safety Improvement Project Guangdong Agricultural Product Quality and Safety Improvement (Demonstration) Project, and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The consulting services aims to strengthen the research and development of high-quality food standards, carry out publicity and promotion activities, and create demonstration and model enterprises. For detailed scope, deliverables, duration, and other specific requirements, please refer to the attached Terms of Reference (TOR).

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment are attached to this request for expressions of interest.

The Guangdong Administration for Market Regulation now invites eligible consultants to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. Terms of Reference

Project on the Construction, Publicity and Promotion of the High-Quality Food Standard System Implemented by Guangdong Administration for Market Regulation

Package  I: Development of High-Quality Food Standards, High-Quality Food Improvement and Model Demonstration Initiative

In order to ensure the effective implementation of Package I (Development of High-Quality Food Standards, High-Quality Food Improvement and Model Demonstration Initiative) under the abovementioned project, and to achieve the targeted objectives of project information technology development, the Guangdong Administration for Market Regulation intends to select and engage qualified service institutions through public procurement to carry out the implementation of this project.

1. Project Background and Overview

The World Bank-financed China Food Safety Demonstration Project took effect on March 21, 2024, with an implementation period ending on March 31, 2029. It aims to comprehensively enhance national and local modern food safety governance capacity. As a key implementing entity of this project in Guangdong Province, the Guangdong Administration for Market Regulation is responsible for project management, procurement management, contract administration, project acceptance, fund reimbursement and payment, as well as reviewing standard development plans and publicity-promotion activity plans, organizing standard reviews, and strictly ensuring project quality.

A total of USD 10 million of World Bank loan is planned for application. Of this amount, Package I (Development of HighQuality Food Standards, HighQuality Food Improvement and Model Demonstration Initiative) under the abovementioned project plans to apply for a World Bank loan of USD 1 million (equivalent to RMB 6.9 million). The engagement of a thirdparty institution serves the following purposes: first, accelerate the development of high-quality food standards, with no fewer than 30 standards completed within two years; second, carry out the highquality food improvement and model demonstration initiatives, including organizing large-scale high-quality food publicity-promotion events (no fewer than six events within two years) and developing model demonstration enterprises for high-quality food (no fewer than six enterprises within two years), and conducting fund management in compliance with relevant requirements.

Expected outcomes of this project include further advancing the development of high-quality food standards in the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area (GBA), and improving the GBA high-quality food standard system. Through advertising, publicity- promotion activities, and the development of model demonstration enterprises for highquality food, stories of highquality food will be well communicated to continuously raise brand recognition and influence, so that highquality food gains wide public acceptance.

The project addresses existing challenges including difficulties in aligning foodrelated rules across the GBA, insufficient coverage in the development of highquality food standards, and inadequate publicitypromotion measures which undermine effective implementation of those standard. Through this project, the Guangdong Administration for Market Regulation will further enhance the core value of high-quality food brands, develop model demonstration enterprises, organize brand-promotion events, advance highquality development of the GBA, facilitate the popularization and application of highquality food standards (namely the GBA Food Standards), expand brand influence, and support the building of a highquality living circle in the Greater Bay Area.

2. Project Objectives

Centered on the core objective of advancing development of high-quality food standards and high-quality food improvement and model demonstration initiative, this project integrates the full-chain traceability platform with "ShangMa Su", the intelligent supervision system of "Internet-based Visualization Kitchen", the real-time emergency dispatching command system, and capacity improvement for food-related personnel under market regulation. It aims to establish a closed-loop full-chain management mechanism covering risk identification, early-warning response and disposal, so as to provide data foundation and institutional guarantee for scientifically calculating outcome indicators such as “proportion of earlywarnings for which mitigation measures have been activated". The core objectives are specified as follows: 

First, expand coverage of high-quality food standards. Building on the 87 high-quality food standards issued up to 2025, further efforts will be intensified to develop highquality food standards,expand coverage of standards, continuously enrich and improve the high-quality food standard system, and meet the demand for highquality and safe food among residents in Guangdong, Hong Kong and Macao.

Second, promote the implementation and application of high-quality food standards. Through highquality food advertising and publicitypromotion activities, as well as highpriority food improvement and model demonstration initiative, enterprises shall be encouraged to formally adopt and apply highquality food standards The project facilitates the extensive circulation of highquality food across online and offline sales channels, and continuously raises the visibility and influence of highquality food..

3. Scope of Services

Total investment for this project amounts to  RMB 6.9 million.

3.1 Scope of Service Recipients

Service recipients cover the Guangdong Administration for Market Regulation, as well as provincial, municipal and district/countylevel market regulation authorities. Target users include the general public and six highquality food manufacturing enterprises, among others.

3.2 Service Content

3.2.1 Engage a thirdparty institution to accelerate the development of high-quality food standards, with no fewer than 30 standards completed within two years. The development of highquality food standards shall comply with relevant documents including the Measures for the Administration of HighQuality Food Standards in the GuangdongHong KongMacao Greater Bay Area, the Specification for the Development of HighQuality Food Standards in the GuangdongHong KongMacao Greater Bay Area (Trial), and the Specification for the Development of GBA Standards for Precooked Dishes. 

Annual plans for the development  of high-quality food standard shall be formulated with the following requirements. Firstly, conduct a comprehensive review on the coverage of issued highquality food standards, identify uncovered areas or weak standardsetting links, and give priority to filling standard gaps for key products and critical links. Secondly, conduct in-depth research on the latest laws, regulations and food standards requirements of Guangdong, Hong Kong and Macao, and give priority to developing the standards for products with distinctive GBA dietary characteristics and large consumption volume. Thirdly, adopt multi-stakeholder participation. Opinions and suggestions from authorities including market regulation, health, and customs shall be fully taken into account.

The standard-development workflow consists of project initiation application, field research, experimental verification, public consultation, review and issuance, Relevant institutions, universities, industry associations and enterprises from Guangdong, Hong Kong and Macao shall participate throughout the process.

3.2.2 .Implement highquality food improvement and model demonstration initiative, including organizing largescale publicity and promotion events for highquality food (no less than six events within two years, with a total attendance of no fewer than 2,000 participants), and developing model demonstration enterprises for highquality food (no less than six enterprises within two years; each enterprise shall have at least two products meeting highquality food standard requirements and prominently display the “GBA Standards” logo on product outer packaging).Model demonstration enterprises shall be large-scale food manufacturers within the GBA that voluntarily adopt the "GBA Standards”, with at least two compliant products. The project contractor shall submit a proposed list of demonstration enterprises for review. The development of demonstration enterprises may only proceed after the Guangdong Administration for Market Regulation confirms compliance with basic eligibility criteria  See Appendix 1 for further details.

Publicity & Promotion

2

Coordinate all publicity, promotion and exchange activities for high-quality food standards

1. Academic background in food science or public health

2. Proven experience in organizing health-themed publicity and communication activities

4

Project Assistants

2

Support the Project Director in daily project delivery

Proven experience in food safety risk assessment, standard development or publicitypromotion activities

6 Facilities and Personnel Provided by the Client

The Client shall provide the following necessary support for smooth project implementation: relevant project documents, reports, annual work plans and other materials; dedicated staff assigned to liaise with the service provider for the implementation of relevant work.

 

Appendix 1: Performance Indicators for Package I

Table 1.1 Summary of Performance Indicators

No.

Task Category

Task Content

Requirements

1

Standard Formulation and Revision

Develop high-quality food standards as required by the Client, with a cumulative minimum of 30 standards within two years (≥26 product standards, ≥4 safety standards). Total quantity shall not be less than 30.

Standard development shall comply with the Regulations on Administration of Group Standards and Specifications for Development of High-Quality Food Standards. Institutions, universities, industry associations and enterprises from Guangdong, Hong Kong and Macao shall participate throughout the development process.

Development workflow  consists of  project initiation application, field research, experimental verification, public consultation, group standard review and issuance, and application for the "GBA Standard" . Submitted standard deliverables shall cover: 1. Lead organization information and standard introduction; 2. Chinese version standard text; 3. English version standard text; 4. Standard Compilation Explanatory Notes; 5.Supporting documents for the standard development process

6.Statement on the application of High-quality food standard

2

Promotion and Application Implementation

Conduct publicitypromotion for highquality food in accordance with the Client’s requirements, organize  no fewer than 6 events within two years, with a total attendance of no fewer than 2,000 participants.

Produce one promotional video for high-quality food standards

3

Design and produce a batch of promotional materials for high-quality food

4

Organize largescale publicitypromotion events for highquality food. Event forms include but are not limited to setting up special exhibition zones in large supermarkets or provinciallevel and above largescale fairs and exhibitions.

5

Develop highquality food model demonstration enterprises. At least 3 enterprises per year, and no fewer than 6 enterprises in total within twoyear period.

Model demonstration enterprises shall cover manufacturing enterprises and trading enterprises:

1. Manufacturing enterprises: At least 2 products shall meet the requirements of highquality food standards; labels shall comply with highquality food standards; the “GBA Standard” logo shall be prominently displayed on product outer packaging in accordance with the logo usage rules of “GBA Standard” issued by Guangdong Administration for Market Regulation; relevant products shall circulate in the market including selfoperated stores or large supermarkets. Shall connect to the highquality food traceability platform, timely upload and update enterprise profile, product stories, product promotional videos, product specifications & shelflife, origin of key raw materials, production licensing information, product inspection reports and other information to realize traceability function for highquality food. Shall cooperate in highquality food publicitypromotion activities

2. Trading enterprises: shall set up special sales zones for highquality food on online platforms and offline stores to carry out centralized publicitypromotion for highquality food

PROJET DE TRANSFORMATION NUMERIQUE « PTN »

 

AVIS DE SOLLICITATION DE MANIFESTATIONS D’INTERET

 ASSISTANCE TECHNIQUE POUR LE SUIVI ET CONTRÔLE DES TRAVAUX DE CONSTRUCTION DU RESEAU BACKBONE EN FIBRE OPTIQUE DE LA DORSALE NATIONALE (11600 Km)

 

P180496

N° Avis : AMI n° ZR-UGP - PTN-553720-CS-QCBS

N° de l’Accord du financement Crédit IDA : 7602-ZR

N° de la Convention de Crédit AFD      : CCD119801 H

N° de référence du marché PPM : ZR-UGP - PTN-553720-CS-QCBS

 

Date : Le 23 septembre 2026

 

Le Gouvernement de la République Démocratique du Congo a reçu un financement de la Banque mondiale d’un montant de 400 millions de dollars américains pour couvrir le coût du Projet de Transformation Numérique de la RDC(PTN) et cofinancé par l'Agence Française de Développement à la hauteur de 100 millions d’euros.

Le projet est géré par une Unité de Gestion du Projet (UGP) qui a été mise en place au sein du Ministère des Postes, Télécommunications (MPT) et a l’intention d’affecter une partie du produit à des services de Consultant firme chargé de l’Assistance Technique pour le suivi et contrôle des travaux de construction du réseau backbone en fibre optique de la dorsale nationale (11600 km).

L’extension de la dorsale nationale en fibre vise à étendre l’accès aux services haut débit et numériques sur l’ensemble du territoire, à désenclaver numériquement les provinces, à interconnecter la RDC avec les pays voisins et les câbles sous-marins, et à fiabiliser le maillage national de la dorsale optique.

L’Unité de Gestion du Projet PTN (« UGP PTN »), agissant pour le compte du MPT, assure la maîtrise d’ouvrage de cette activité et la gestion des accords conclus avec les Bailleurs.

La construction et l’exploitation du réseau sont organisées selon un modèle de concession (Partenariat Public-Privé) avec financement d’appoint (gap d’investissements) pour une durée de vingt (20) ans. Le réseau est réparti en quatre (4) lots géographiques distincts qui seront attribués à l’issue d’un appel d’offres international à une étape et deux enveloppes.

L’objectif global de la mission est d’assurer, en toute indépendance et pour le compte du Maître d’Ouvrage, le suivi et le contrôle technique des travaux de construction du réseau de fibres optiques sur les quatre lots, afin de garantir la conformité des ouvrages aux spécifications techniques, aux normes de qualité, aux exigences environnementales et sociales et aux délais, et de fournir au Maître d’Ouvrage l’assurance technique nécessaire à la libération progressive du financement d’appoint. Le Consultant exerce également un rôle de conseil auprès du Maître d’Ouvrage dans la définition des standards des installations et la gestion des risques tout au long de la mise en œuvre du Projet.

La mission couvre les travaux réalisés par les Concessionnaires – directement ou par l’intermédiaire de leurs constructeurs et sous-traitants – depuis les études d’exécution et les réceptions usine jusqu’à la réception définitive des ouvrages, pour les composantes passive et active du réseau.

 

Le démarrage de la mission est prévu au mois de juin 2027 pour une durée de quarante (40) mois.

Les termes de référence complets pour le poste ainsi que l’attestation d’intégrité de l’AFD sont disponibles sur le site de mediacongo.net : www.mediacongo.net, sous l’onglet « Offres d’emploi » et sur le site de l’UG PTN : www.ugptn.cd.

 

L’Unité de Gestion de Projet PTN invite dès à présent les firmes de consultants admissibles (« Consultants ») à faire part de leur intérêt à fournir les Services. Les Consultants intéressés doivent fournir des informations démontrant qu’ils possèdent les qualifications requises et l’expérience pertinente pour exécuter les Services.

 Les critères d’évaluation de manifestations d’intérêt pour l’établissement de la liste restreinte sont les suivants :

  • Une expérience confirmée dans le suivi et le contrôle de projets de réseaux à fibres optiques ;
  • La maîtrise des normes et techniques de pose, de raccordement et de mesure (passif) et des équipements de transmission et de supervision (actif) ;
  • Une expérience en gestion de projets d’infrastructures de télécommunications et en réglementation/conformité du secteur ;
  • Une expérience pertinente en Afrique, dont au minimum deux (2) missions similaires en nature, envergure ou complexité, justifiées par des Attestations de Bonne Exécution (ou équivalent) au cours des cinq (5) dernières années ;
  • Une expérience documentée de la gestion des aspects environnementaux et sociaux selon les standards de la Banque mondiale (NES), y compris VBG/EAS/HS et PAR (NES 5) ;
  • Une bonne maîtrise des outils de mesure et logiciels de suivi (dont SIG) ;
  • De solides capacités d’analyse, de reporting et de coordination multi-lots ;
  • La maîtrise de la langue française.
  • Une bonne connaissance des normes ISO \ UIT-T dans le domaine des télécommunications et réseaux à fibres optiques.
  • Une expérience de projets financés par la Banque mondiale, l’AFD ou d’autres institutions financières internationales, ainsi qu’une connaissance du contexte de la République Démocratique du Congo, constitueront des atouts.

Les experts clés ne seront pas évalués à cette étape.

 

L’attention des Consultants intéressés est attirée sur la Section III, paragraphes, 3.14, 3.16 et 3.17 du « Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs de FPI » de la Banque mondiale, Septième Edition, Septembre 25 (Règlement de passation des marchés), qui énonce la politique de la Banque mondiale en matière de conflits d’intérêts. Le candidat devra compléter l’Attestation d’intégrité de l’AFD et la retourner dûment signée accompagnée de sa manifestation d’intérêts.

 

Les Consultants peuvent s’associer à d’autres firmes pour améliorer leurs qualifications, mais ils doivent indiquer clairement si l’association prend la forme d’un groupement et/ou d’une sous-traitance. Dans le cas d’un groupement, tous les membres du groupement d’entreprises seront solidairement responsables de l’ensemble du contrat, s’ils sont sélectionnés.

 

Un Consultant(firme) sera sélectionné selon la méthode de Sélection Fondée sur la Qualité et le Coût (SFQC) par mise en concurrence ouverte internationale telle que décrite dans le Règlement de passation des marchés susmentionné.

 

Les Consultants intéressés peuvent obtenir des informations supplémentaires à l’adresse physique ci-dessous ou à l’adresse électronique recrutement@ugpatn.cd chaque jour ouvrable de 9 heures à 16 heures locales.

 

L’UG PTN se réserve le droit de vérifier l’authenticité des informations fournies par les candidats aux fins de la présente sélection. Les candidats ayant fourni des informations tronquées ne seront pas retenus pour la suite du processus de passation des marchés.

Les Manifestations d’Intérêt, écrites en langue française, doivent être déposées physiquement à l’adresse ci-dessous en personne, par courrier accompagné d’une version électronique en format Word ou Pdf copiable sur une clé USB ou de préférence, envoyées par courrier électronique en format Pdf copiable à l’adresse mail : recrutement@ugpatn.cd au plus tard le 14 octobre 2026 à 14h00’ heures locales (TU+1) et porter clairement la mention :« AMI n° ZR-UGP - PTN-553720-CS-QCBS :Recrutement d’un Consultant firme chargé de  l’Assistance Technique l’Assistance Technique  pour le suivi et contrôle des travaux de construction du réseau backbone en fibre optique de la dorsale nationale (11600 km)»..

 

 

Noel Jean David LITANGA SANGU PAMBA

 

 

                Coordonnateur

Government of Nepal

Kathmandu Valley Water Supply Management Board (KVWSMB)

Kathmandu Valley Water Security Improvement Project (KV WaSIP) – Sisneri Water Supply Project

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (REOI)

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

COUNTRY: Nepal

Name of the Project: Kathmandu Valley Water Security Improvement Project (KV WaSIP) – Sisneri Water Supply Project

Grant No: E757-NP

Assignment Title: Consulting Service for the Preparation of an Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA), an Environmental and Social Impact Assessment (ESIA), and other Environmental and Social Documents Required for the Project

Reference No.: NP-KVWSMB-572486-CS-CQS

First Date of Publication: 23rd September 2026

1. The Government of Nepal (GoN) has received financing from the World Bank toward the preparation and implementation of the Kathmandu Valley Water Security Improvement Project (KV WaSIP) – Sisneri Water Supply Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

2. The consulting services (“the Services”) include Preparation of an Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA), an Environmental and Social Impact Assessment (ESIA) and other Environmental and Social Documents Required for the Project. A total of 97 person-months of experts is estimated. The assignment is expected to commence in January 2027 and will have an implementation period of 16 months. The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at the following website: www.kvwsmb.org.np.

3. The Kathmandu Valley Water Supply Management Board (KVWSMB) now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the above consulting services. Interested Consultants shall provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria for the qualifications and experience of the firm are as follows: 

a. Core Business and General Experience:

The consulting firm shall be duly registered and have at least 10 years of demonstrated experience in EIA/ESIA/CIA, dam engineering, water resources, water supply, hydropower, civil engineering, hydraulic infrastructure, or related fields. The firm shall have successfully or substantially completed at least five (5) relevant EIA/ESIA assignments for major infrastructure projects, with each assignment meeting either of the following: (i) consulting contract value of at least NRs. 10 million for primarily environmental/social services; or (ii) consulting contract value of at least NRs. 30 million for feasibility study and/or detailed engineering design combined with environmental/social services.

b. Specific Experience (Last 10 years):

  • At least two (2) EIA/ESIA/CIA assignments for water resources or water supply projects, meeting the specified minimum contract value of NRs. 10 million for environmental/social services or NRs. 30 million for feasibility/design combined with environmental/social services;
  • At least one (1) EIA/ESIA/CIA assignment for a dam, reservoir or water-storage project with dam height of at least 35 meters;
  • At least one (1) Detailed EIA/ESIA/CIA assignment for a water resources project in the hilly or mountainous region of Nepal; and
  • At least one (1) assignment involving Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) or Environmental and Social Impact Assessment (ESIA) financed by or implemented with the support of the World Bank or another multilateral or bilateral development partner in the water resources, water supply, irrigation, hydropower or other water related infrastructure sector

c. Technical and Managerial Capability:
The firm shall demonstrate adequate technical and managerial capacity to undertake the assignment. Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

4. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.13, 3.15, and 3.16 of the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, Seventh Edition (September 2025), setting forth the World Bank's policy on Conflict of Interest.

5. Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected. A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Consultants Qualifications-based Selection (CQS) method as set out in the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers”, Seventh Edition (September 2025).

6. Further information and the Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment may be obtained during office hours from the address below.

7. Expressions of interest must be delivered in a written form to the address below (in person or by mail or by e-mail) by 14th October 2026, 14.00 Hrs.

Memo No. 46.06.2000.000. 335.28.0034.26-171                                                 Date:  21.09.2026

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

Consultancy Services for Construction Supervision, Social Intermediation, Community Mobilization, and Awareness Raising for Improved Water Supply and Sanitation Services in Low-Income Communities (LICs) in Chattogram City

(National - Package Reference: CWSIP/S8)

  1. The Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh has received financing from the International Development Association toward the cost of the Chattogram Water Supply Improvement Project (CWSIP). Chattogram Water Supply and Sewerage Authority (CWASA), the implementing agency, intends to apply part of the proceeds of this financing to payments under the above-mentioned consulting assignment.
  2. The objective of the assignment is to support CWASA in implementing water-supply and non-network sanitation investments in selected low-income communities (LICs) in Chattogram City. The services combine construction supervision, social intermediation, community mobilization, awareness raising, stakeholder coordination, and the establishment of practical operations and maintenance (O&M) arrangements. The assignment is intended to ensure site readiness; secure the necessary community, landowner, and institutional agreements; supervise and document the works; establish community structures; agree O&M arrangements before handover; and provide CWASA with timely information for managing implementation, risks, service commencement, and post-commissioning support.
  3. The assignment is expected to be implemented over 36 months. The complete Terms of Reference (TOR) is available at https://ctg-wasa.org.bd. It may also be obtained via email by sending a request to cwsip.cwasa@gmail.com.
  4. CWASA now invites eligible national consulting firms ("Consultants") to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants shall provide information demonstrating that they possess the required qualifications and relevant experience. The EOI shall be supported by verifiable information on completed assignments.

Qualification requirements

  • 10 years of demonstrated organizational experience in participatory planning, awareness generation, behavior change communication, and community mobilization with poor communities in Bangladesh, preferably in WASH, public health, environmental health, or urban resilience;
  • Five years of demonstrated experience working with urban poor communities or LICs on water supply, sanitation, FSM, shared sanitation, or related service delivery arrangements in Bangladesh;
  • Demonstrated experience coordinating with city agencies, utilities, municipalities/ pourashavas, WASAs, district administrations, contractors, CBOs, NGOs, or landowners for implementation of community-level infrastructure or service-delivery assignments; and
  • Demonstrated capacity to manage multidisciplinary field teams for construction supervision support, community facilitation, reporting, and coordination across multiple sites.

Information to be included in the EOI

  • a concise firm profile and evidence of legal registration and authorization to operate in Bangladesh;
  • details of relevant assignments, including the client, country and location, period, status, scope of services, the firm's role, and supporting evidence;
  • a description of the firm's organizational, financial-management, documentation, reporting, and quality-management systems;
  • evidence of its capacity to deploy and manage multidisciplinary teams across multiple field locations.
  1. The firm assessed as having the best qualifications and relevant experience will be invited to submit a combined technical and financial proposal for negotiation.
  2. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraphs 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, which set out the World Bank's policy on conflict of interest.
  3. A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Consultant's Qualifications-based Selection (CQS) method set out in the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, Fifth Edition, September 2023.
  4. Expression of Interest (EoI) (both hard copy and soft copy preferable) needs to be submitted (either in person or by mail or by e-mail) to the following address by 15:00 hours (BST) (GMT+6) on or before October 14, 2026. The envelope shall be clearly marked: "Expression of Interest - Package CWSIP/S8."
  5. EOIs received after the submission deadline will not be considered. CWASA may cancel the selection process only in accordance with the applicable Procurement Regulations.

 

 

 

 

 

(Md. Rejaul Ahsan Chowdhury)

Project Director

Chattogram Water Supply Improvement Project (CWSIP)

Chattogram WASA

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

Consultancy Services for Site Assessment, Design, and Supervision of Upgrading Investments In Harvest and Post-Harvest Fisheries Infrastructure: Calliaqua Fisheries Centre.

Reference No: SVGUBEC-C-QCBS-8

The Government of Saint Vincent and the Grenadines (GoSVG) has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the SVG Unleashing the Blue Economy of the Caribbean (UBEC) project, and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The Government of SVG (GoSVG) has established a Project Implementation Unit (PIU) at the Ministry of Tourism, Civil Aviation, and Sustainable Development (MoTCASD) responsible for implementing the UBEC project national-level activities and coordinating with relevant ministries.

The consulting services (“the Services”) include; to provide the Government of SVG and the UBEC Project Implementation Unit (PIU) with the technical, financial, and operational evidence base required to make sound, sustainable investment decisions for the Calliaqua Fisheries Centre and, based on these decisions, to execute detailed design and construction supervision to the standard required for a durable, well-maintained public fisheries asset.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at the following website: https://procurement.gov.vc/eprocure/index.php/current-bids 

The MoTCASD, in conjunction with the Ministry of Fisheries, Marine and Land Conservation and Climate Resilience, now invite eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

The shortlisting criteria are:

  1. The consulting firm should have expertise in fisheries infrastructure development, assessment and rehabilitation, strong knowledge of marine and coastal engineering principles, proficiency in technical specifications writing including Bills of Quantities and Procurement documentation, and a demonstrated understanding of renewable energy integration in fisheries infrastructure.
  2. The team shall include professionals with experience in engineering design, the conduction of root cause analyses, and stakeholder engagement and training.

Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality and Cost-Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

REPUBLIC OF THE GAMBIA

The Gambia Water and Sanitation Project (WASAP)

Project ID: P513113

Assignment Title:

Consultancy Services for Feasibility Studies, Detailed Engineering Design, Procurement Support, Construction Supervision, and Defects Liability Support for Urban Water Supply Systems in Kombo East and Urban Sanitation Infrastructure in Kotu and Banjul

Reference No.: GM-NAWEC-565968-CS-QCBS

The Republic of The Gambia has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Gambia Water and Sanitation Project (WASAP) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services for Feasibility Studies, Detailed Engineering Design, Procurement Support, Construction Supervision, and Defects Liability Support for Urban Water Supply Systems in Kombo East and Urban Sanitation Infrastructure in Kotu and Banjul.

The Greater Banjul Area is the country’s principal urban and economic center. Urban water services face major challenges including production constraints, intermittent supply, ageing infrastructure, limited storage capacity, and high levels of non-revenue water. Similarly, sanitation services in Banjul and Kotu are constrained by deteriorated sewerage assets, underperforming wastewater treatment facilities, and inadequate fecal sludge management infrastructure.  WASAP will support the Government of The Gambia in addressing these challenges through investments aimed at improving service coverage, reliability, resilience, and sustainability of water supply and sanitation services.

The assignment will support the preparation and implementation of priority investments in urban water supply and urban sanitation infrastructure, including:

  • Urban water supply investments in Kombo East and Brikama East comprising boreholes, treatment facilities, storage reservoirs, transmission pipelines, distribution networks, household connections, SCADA systems, and power supply facilities; and
  • Urban sanitation investments including rehabilitation and expansion of wastewater and sewerage infrastructure in Kotu and Banjul, fecal sludge treatment facilities, pumping stations, and associated infrastructure.

Scope of the Services

The consulting services will be undertaken in five phases:

Phase 1: Feasibility Study

  • Review existing studies, plans, records, GIS data and infrastructure information.
  • Conduct socio-economic, service area, demand and affordability assessments.
  • Undertake detailed feasibility studies for urban water supply and sanitation investments.
  • Assess climate resilience, environmental and social requirements, institutional arrangements, technical options and implementation strategies.
  • Conduct economic and financial analyses, including lifecycle costing and investment prioritization.
  • Prepare feasibility reports and preliminary designs.

Phase 2: Detailed Engineering Design

  • Undertake topographic, cadastral, geotechnical, laboratory and utility investigations.
  • Prepare detailed engineering designs for:
    • Water supply facilities including boreholes, treatment systems, reservoirs, transmission mains, distribution networks and SCADA.
    • Sanitation facilities include wastewater treatment systems, fecal sludge treatment plants, sewer networks, pumping stations and sea outfall improvements.
  • Prepare design calculations, drawings, technical specifications, cost estimates, bills of quantities, and O&M documentation.
  • Prepare procurement-ready engineering packages.

Phase 3: Procurement Support

  • Prepare complete bidding documents and technical specifications.
  • Participate in pre-bid meetings and site visits.
  • Provide support during bid evaluation and contract award processes.
  • Respond to technical clarifications and prepare addenda where required.

Phase 4: Construction Supervision and Contract Administration

  • Supervise construction works and administer contracts.
  • Monitor quality assurance, environmental and social compliance, occupational health and safety, cost and schedule performance.
  • Review contractor submissions and oversee testing and commissioning.
  • Support handover and completion.

Phase 5: Defects Liability Support

  • Conduct inspections during the defect’s liability period.
  • Verify correction of defects.
  • Support final completion and contract close-out.

Duration

The estimated duration of the assignment is 46.5 months, including feasibility studies, design, procurement support, construction supervision, and defects liability support.

National Water and Electricity Company Limited (NAWEC), through the WASAP Project Implementation Unit (PIU), now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

Shortlisting Criteria

Interested firms should demonstrate:

  • At least 15 years of experience in water supply and sanitation engineering.
  • At least 10 years of experience in feasibility studies, detailed design, and construction supervision of urban water and sanitation infrastructure.
  • Demonstrated experience in water treatment facilities, transmission and distribution networks, reservoirs, SCADA systems, wastewater treatment facilities, sewerage systems, pumping stations, and fecal sludge treatment infrastructure.
  • Successful completion of at least two comparable assignments financed by multilateral development partners within the last seven years.
  • Demonstrated experience in Africa and familiarity with international forms of contract including FIDIC or equivalent.
  • Demonstrated quality assurance, environmental and social management, and occupational health and safety systems.

The qualifications and experience of Key Experts shall not be included in the shortlisting criteria. Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

THE REVOLUTIONARY GOVERNMENT OF ZANZIBAR

MINISTRY OF BLUE ECONONMY AND FISHERIES

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST

 

Country: United Republic of Tanzania.

Name of project: Tanzania scaling up sustainable marine fisheries and aquaculture management (TASFAM) project (p.179969).

Assignment title: Consultancy Services for Conduct full Socio-Economic Impact Assessments in Existing and New MCA’s.

REF. NO.: TZ-MBEF-561671-CS-CDS

This request for expression of interests follows the General Procurement Notice for the Tanzania scaling up sustainable marine fisheries and aquaculture management (TASFAM) project which appeared in the UN Development Business Online on 5th June 2025.

The Revolutionary Government of Zanzibar through the United Republic of Tanzania has received financing from the World Bank towards the cost of Tanzania Scaling up Sustainable Marine Fisheries and Aquaculture Management (TASFAM) Project and it intends to apply part of the proceeds of the financing to cover eligible payments under the contract for Consultancy Services for Conduct full Socio-Economic Impact Assessments in Existing and New MCA’s.

The objective of the assignment is to evaluate the legal and socio-economic context of the MPA/MCA including natural resource and land-use rights, community access patterns, and any historical or legacy issues, to establish a comprehensive household-level socio-economic baseline of affected communities and assess the anticipated positive and negative impacts of access restrictions on livelihoods, income, food and nutrition security.

 

The consultant shall be required to carry out the following activities: -

  • Conduct a comprehensive socio-economic assessment of communities affected by or dependent on the MPA/MCA.
  • Assess the potential socio-economic impacts of existing and proposed access restrictions.
  • Assess the legal, institutional and governance arrangements governing natural resource use, fisheries and community access.
  • Develop an appropriate monitoring and evaluation framework with measurable indicators for tracking implementation and outcomes.

Detailed information on the scope can be obtained in the terms of references (TOR) available to the following website:  https://tasfam.blueeconomysmz.go.tz.

The Ministry of Blue Economy and Fisheries Zanzibar now invites eligible consulting firms to submit their expression of interests in providing these services.  Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications, relevant experience and key experts to perform the services. The qualification and shortlisting criteria shall include: -

  • The firm shall demonstrate a portfolio of at least 5 assignments in the preparation of RAPs, ARAPs, TRPs, or equivalent social safeguards instruments for World Bank-financed or equivalent projects in Sub-Saharan Africa.
  • Experience in the fisheries, coastal, or blue economy sector is an advantage.
  • The firm shall have demonstrated experience of working with communities dependent on natural resources, particularly in contexts involving temporary or permanent displacement.
  • Qualified team of personnel. The firm should indicate list and qualifications of key personnel proposed for this assignment (Cvs are optional).

Attention of interested consultants is drawn to section III paragraph 3.11,3.12 and 3.13 of the World Bank’s procurement regulations for IPF Borrowers Sixth Edition February 2025.

The People's Republic of Bangladesh has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Host and Rohingya Enhancement of Lives Project (HELP) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services for Development of a detailed Strategic Environmental Assessment (SEA) for the existing and proposed Policies, Plans, Programs, and Projects in the region of Cox’sBazar District with adjoining Marine and Marine Coastal areas  as well as other impacted areas and prepare a Strategic Environmental Management Plan (SEMP) with future intervension to manage and restore the environment and ecosystem in the impacted area.

 

  1. The broad scope of consulting services (“the Services”) includes but not limited to:
  • Inception
  • Screening
  • Scoping
  • A report on Strategic Environmental Assessment (SEA) along with the detailed analysis of the PPPPs
  • Strategic Environmental Management Plan (SEMP)
  • Draft Final SEA Report including SEMP
  1. The objectives of the consultancy services are to come-up with the cumulative environmental impacts of the existing and proposed Policies, Plans, Programs, and Projects (PPPPs) in Cox’s Bazar district including Teknaf Peninsula and other FDMNs-impacted areas so that the GoB can address them at the earliest phase of decision making alongside economic and social considerations. The specific objectives are:
  • Consideration of environmental and socio-economic consequences of existing and proposed PPPs (national and Cox’s Bazar district including Teknaf Peninsula and other FDMNs impacted areas) that cover the target area of this assignment and promoting that these issues be addressed when formulating and implementing future, as well as existing and proposed PPPs to promote sustainable development in the target area and conservation of their environmental and ecological value;
  • Identification of key stakeholders relevant to selected sectors and organizing consultation meetings to obtain knowledge on existing bio-physical settings and socio-economic conditions, impacts of current and proposed developments, and potential strategies for future development of the Cox’s Bazar district-Teknaf Peninsula and other FDMNs impacted areas;
  • Development of alternative strategies to minimize the direct/indirect, domestic/transboundary and cumulative impacts of development on the study area of the Chattogram division;
  • Prepare a SEMP with potential recommendations to improve environmental performance management in both the public and private sectors with regard to current and future development activities as well as to manage and restore the environment and ecosystem in the impacted area.
  • Formulation of a comprehensive monitoring framework as part of the Strategic Environmental Management Plan (SEMP) for the study area of the Chattogram division including Cox’s Bazar district-Teknaf Peninsula and other FDMNs impacted areas to support decision making and monitoring of the implementation of PPPs that are likely to affect the environment and socio-economic conditions of the target area.

Republic of Mozambique

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

 

Grant No IDA E212

 

Assignment Title: Consultancy to Support the Operationalization of the Complaints Resolution System (CRS) and the Action Plan for the Prevention of Risks and Response to GBV, SEA and SH in the Project’s Implementation Areas

 

 

Activity No. MZ-MJD- 567158-CS-QCBS

 

 

The Government of Mozambique (GoM), through the National Youth Institute (INJ) under the supervision of the Ministry of Youth and Sports (MJD), and with the support of the World Bank, is implementing the “East Africa Girls' Empowerment and Resilience” (EAGER) investment project. This regional initiative, financed by the World Bank and implemented in partnership with the Africa Union, aims to increase girls’ and women’s educational attainment and earnings in the program areas, and to strengthen the institutional capacity to implement gender-equality policies.

In Mozambique, the EAGER investment operation (2024 to 2029) is implemented jointly by the Ministry of Labor, Gender, and Social Action (MTGAS) and the MJD.

 

Component 4. Support for Project Implementation. This component will support the project’s implementing agencies (MJD and MTGAS) in designing and implementing multisectoral activities at national level and within the regional context. The project will fund the strengthening of the existing Project Management Units (PMUs) within the two institutions responsible for the day-to-day management and implementation of the project; operational costs; equipment; and training.

 

These Terms of Reference refer to the selection of a Consultant To support the project’s implementing agencies (MJD and MTGAS) in operationalizing the Complaints Resolution System (CRS), which is sensitive to Gender-Based Violence, Exploitation and Sexual Abuse and Sexual Harassment (GBV/SEA/SH), Violence Against Children (VaC), in particular child sexual abuse, forced and early marriages, and child labour, including the referral and monitoring of cases to ensure access to holistic support services for survivors in the project’s implementation areas (115 districts across 11 provinces).

 

The main tasks of this team are as follows:

  1. To develop and implement a communication strategy for the widespread promotion of the Complaints Resolution System;
  2. Conduct awareness-raising campaigns and sessions to prevent and mitigate the risks of GBV/SEA/SH in schools, communities, CBO’s and other organisations, and for the project’s other stakeholders;
  3. To supervise, evaluate and monitor the implementation processes of the CRS and sensitive cases;
  4. Identify, receive and record all complaints and cases of GBV, and refer them to local GBV service providers;
  5. Assist victims with their social reintegration (school, family and community).

 

 

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment and further information can be obtained via email at the following address: eagerprocurement@gmail.com

 

The INJ now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

 

The shortlisting criteria are:

 

  • A minimum of 6 years’ experience in the implementation and/or strengthening of Grievance Redress Systems, including the design of operational workflows, accessible and inclusive reporting channels, and referral and response mechanisms;
  • A minimum of 7 years’ experience in managing sensitive cases, ensuring confidentiality and a victim-centred approach, and in the development and implementation of Action Plans for the prevention of and response to GBV/SEA/SH;
  • At least 7 years’ experience in delivering training and capacity-building for technical teams, implementing partners and stakeholders on GBV/SEA/SH and the functioning of the CRS;
  • Experience of working with vulnerable communities, including women, girls and other at-risk groups, and the ability to liaise with service providers (health, psychosocial support, legal aid) and institutional referral mechanisms;
  • Experience in monitoring and evaluation, including defining indicators, data collection and the preparation of technical reports.

Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage. 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.15, 3.19, and 3.20 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” September 2023 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

pendientes.Texto:
SOLLICITATION DE MANIFESTATIONS D’INTERET

 

Pays : Burundi

Nom du Projet : Projet pour l’Emploi et la Transformation Economique (PRETE)

Numéro de Prêt/Crédit/Don:  Don IDA N° E-2650-BI

N° du projet: P172988

 

Intitule de la mission : Spécialiste en Micro, Petites et Moyennes Entreprises (MPME) du PRETE

Numéro de référence (selon le Plan de Passation des marchés) : BI-ADB-571156-CS-INDV

La République du Burundi a obtenu un financement de la Banque mondiale pour couvrir le coût du Projet pour l’Emploi et la Transformation Economique (PRETE), et a l'intention d’utiliser une partie du montant de ce don pour effectuer les paiements au titre du contrat suivant : « Spécialiste en Micro, Petites et Moyennes Entreprises (MPME) du PRETE ».

Les services de consultants (« les services ») consistent à appuyer techniquement l’UGP du PRETE dans la préparation, la coordination, le suivi et la qualité de la mise en œuvre de la Composante 1 « Accès des MPME aux marchés et développement des chaînes de valeur ». Le/la Spécialiste en Micro, Petites et Moyennes Entreprises (MPME) du PRETE veillera à la cohérence et à la qualité technique des activités conduites au titre des sous-composantes 1.1, 1.2 et 1.3 et à leur contribution à l’atteinte des résultats du projet.

La durée des prestations s’étend jusqu’à la date de clôture du Projet (29/12/2028) à partir de la notification du contrat.

Les termes de référence détaillés (TdR) pour la mission peuvent être obtenus à l'adresse indiquée ci-dessous ou par mail.

L’Unité de gestion du PRETE invite maintenant les candidats éligibles (« Consultants individuels ») à manifester leur intérêt à fournir les Services. Les candidats intéressés doivent fournir toutes les informations nécessaires démontrant qu'ils possèdent les qualifications requises et l'expérience pertinente pour exécuter les services. Le Consultant devra répondre aux critères suivants :

  • Être titulaire au minimum d’un Master en sciences économiques, gestion, administration des affaires, entrepreneuriat, sciences du développement, sciences sociales ou dans une autre discipline pertinente ;
  • Avoir au moins cinq (5) années d’expérience professionnelle pertinente dans le développement, l’accompagnement ou l’appui aux Micro, Petites et Moyennes Entreprises (MPME), dont une expérience significative au Burundi ;
  • Justifier d’une expérience avérée dans la conception, la préparation, la coordination, la mise en œuvre et/ou le suivi de programmes en faveur des MPME, notamment dans les domaines de l’accès aux marchés, des chaînes de valeur, du développement des fournisseurs, de l’accompagnement entrepreneurial, du renforcement des capacités et de l’adoption des technologies ;
  • Avoir une expérience pratique en matière d’accès des MPME aux infrastructures productives, d’amélioration de la productivité et de la compétitivité, de certification et de qualité, de développement de partenariats et de mise en relation commerciale ;
  • Avoir une bonne connaissance de l’écosystème du secteur privé et des MPME au Burundi, notamment des institutions publiques, chambres de commerce, organisations professionnelles, institutions financières, entreprises principales, prestataires de services et structures d’appui aux entreprises ;
  • Posséder une bonne compréhension des principales contraintes auxquelles sont confrontées les MPME burundaises, notamment en matière d’accès aux marchés, d’intégration dans les chaînes de valeur, d’infrastructures productives, de financement, de technologies et transformation numérique, de compétences managériales et techniques, de normes et certification, ainsi que de résilience au changement climatique ;
  • Avoir une expérience de collaboration avec des institutions publiques, des organisations du secteur privé, des chambres de commerce, des associations professionnelles, des partenaires techniques et financiers et/ou des programmes de développement ;
  • Une expérience dans la préparation de PTBA, de termes de référence, de dossiers techniques et dans la collaboration avec des projets financés par la Banque mondiale ou d’autres partenaires au développement constitue un atout ;
  • Avoir une bonne capacité d’organisation du travail, de planification, d’analyse, de rédaction de rapports et de préparation de documents techniques ;
  • Être capable d’effectuer des missions sur le terrain et de travailler avec des équipes, partenaires et bénéficiaires dans différents contextes ;
  • Avoir une bonne maîtrise des logiciels informatiques standards, notamment Word, Excel, PowerPoint et des outils usuels de communication et de collaboration en ligne ;
  • Avoir une intégrité professionnelle, un sens élevé des responsabilités et de bonnes aptitudes à travailler en équipe ;
  • Avoir de bonnes aptitudes en communication écrite et orale et un bon sens des relations humaines ;
  • Avoir une bonne connaissance du français écrit et parlé et une bonne maîtrise de l’anglais.

L'attention des Consultants intéressés est attirée sur la Section III, paragraphes 3.14, 3.16 et 3.17 du « Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projets d’Investissement FPI » de septembre 2023 (« Règlement »), énonçant la politique de la Banque mondiale en matière de conflits d'intérêts.

Un consultant sera sélectionné conformément à la méthode de Sélection des Consultants Individuels avec approche ouverte nationale, énoncée dans le Règlement de passation des marchés de la Banque mondiale pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le (FPI), Edition de septembre 2023 et conformément aux critères exigés par les termes de référence.

De plus amples informations peuvent être obtenues à l'adresse ci-dessous pendant les heures de bureau, du Lundi au Vendredide 08 heures à 12 heures et de 14 heures à 18 heures.

Les manifestations d'intérêt rédigées en Français et portant la mention : « Réponse à l’Avis de Sollicitation de Manifestations d'intérêt pour le recrutement d’un(e) Spécialiste en Micro, Petites et Moyennes Entreprises (MPME) du PRETE » doivent être remises par écrit à l'adresse ci-dessous (en personne, ou par courrier, ou par e-mail au plus tard le 16 octobre 2026 à 16 heures, heure de Bujumbura ».

 

À l'attention de : Mme Béatrice NZEYIMANA, Coordonnatrice du PRETE

Immeuble La Tulipe, Bureau du projet PRETE

1, Rue Inkondo, Boulevard Mwezi Gisabo, Mutanga - Nord

Bujumbura, Burundi

Tél : +257 22 21 16 68

Courriel : bnzeyimana@prete.bi avec copie obligatoire à gniyongabo@prete.bi et jcbigirindavyi@prete.bi.

Site Web : www.prete.bi
