REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (REOI)

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

Country: Mongolia

Project Title: Fifth Energy Sector Project (ESP-5)

Grant No.: GFPP Grant No. TF0C8834

Assignment Title: Detailed Engineering Design and Preparation of Bidding Documents for the Expansion and Modernization of the Power Transmission and Distribution Grid in Ulaanbaatar and Surrounding Areas – Lot 1

Reference No.: MN-MOE-ESP5-CS-QCBS-LOT1

The Government of Mongolia has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Fifth Energy Sector Project (ESP5) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services for the following consulting services.

The consulting services (“Services”) include preparing the Detailed Engineering Design for the Expansion of the Electricity Transmission and Distribution System for Lot 1. The assignment will last sixteen (16) months. During this period, the Consultant shall prepare comprehensive detailed engineering designs and draft bidding documents for eleven (11) identified sub-projects under Lot 1. The Services shall be carried out in accordance with the applicable laws and regulations of Mongolia, relevant international and national technical standards, and the World Bank’s Environmental, Social, Health, and Safety (ESHS) requirements.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment are available at:

https://docs.google.com/document/d/1k_Y0V5s0IlTTuYfPKud8JvhzGIkEYaA_dYyVcRwOXlo/edit?usp=sharing

The Ministry of Energy now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to express their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they are qualified to perform the Services, including:

  • Relevant experience in assignments of similar nature, scope, and complexity, particularly in detailed design of power transmission lines and substations;
  • Firm’s core business, years in operation, and technical and managerial capabilities relevant to the assignment;
  • Organizational capacity, availability of qualified personnel, quality assurance and monitoring approaches, and resources available to undertake the Services; and
  • Other supporting documentation demonstrating the firm’s qualifications and experience, as appropriate.

Shortlisting criteria are as follows:

Interested firms must provide evidence demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services, including:

  1. General Experience: Minimum seven (7) years of continuous experience in the energy sector, with focus on the detailed engineering design of power transmission lines and substations.
  2. Specific Experience: Successful completion of at least two (2) contracts within the last ten (10) years involving the preparation of Detailed Engineering Designs for substations, overhead transmission lines, and cable lines rated at 110 kV or above, which shall have been approved by the relevant State Expert Review authority. Experience in projects financed by international financial institutions (IFIs) will be considered an advantage.
  3. Licensing Requirement: The firm shall hold valid licenses specified in Articles 8.1.3.1 and 8.1.14.7 of the Law of Mongolia on Permits (for high-complexity facility construction and engineering design).
  4. Organizational and Technical Capability: Information demonstrating the firm’s organizational structure, quality management systems, technical resources, professional capabilities and managerial capacity relevant to the assignment.

Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” February 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality and Cost Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers. Only shortlisted Consultants will be invited to submit a technical and financial proposal.

Expressions of interest must be delivered in written form to the address below by e-mail at munkhbadral@energy.gov.mn no later than 17:00 hours (local time) on 16 October 2026.

Address for Submission:

Attention:        Mr. Munkhbadral.P, Policy and Planning Department, Ministry of Energy of Mongolia

Address:         Room No.213, Government Building 14, Chinggis Avenue, Khan-Uul District, Ulaanbaatar 17060, Mongolia

Tel. number:    +976-51-263094

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES/FIRMS SELECTION)

 HASHEMITE KINGDOM OF JORDAN

JORDAN WATER SECTOR EFFICIENCY PROGRAM

IBRD Loan No. 9560-JO, CFF TF No. TF0C1892, AFD No. CJO 1141 01P

 Assignment Title: Consultancy Services for Dam Safety Archiving, Information Management and Decision Support System

Reference No.: JO-JVA-064-CS-QCBS

 

The Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan, Ministry of Water and Irrigation, has received financing from the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (World Bank), the Agence Française de Développement (AFD) and Global Concessional Financing Facility (GCFF) in the amount of US$ 300,000,000 toward the cost of the Jordan Water Sector Efficiency Project, and it intends to apply part of the proceeds to payments for consulting services to be procured under this project.

The consulting services (“the Services”) is to design, develop and operationalize an archiving, information management and decision support system for dam safety that can encompass the full lifecycle of dams in the portfolio. This includes the following main tasks:

  1. Inception Phase
  2. Current State Analysis
  3. Employer’s Requirements Definition
  4. Data and Information Management System
  5. Asset Management System
  6. Decision Support System
  7. Preparation of Bidding documents and Completion.

 

The Detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at the following website:

https://www.mwi.gov.jo/Ar/Tenders

The Jordan Valley Authority (JVA) now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

A consulting firm is allowed to submit the expression of interest alone if it considers itself to be fully qualified on its own for the assignment, as it is not mandatory for consultants to associate with any other firm(s), whether foreign or local. Alternatively.

 If consultants themselves choose to associate to enhance their qualifications and capability for the assignment, then such associations may either be as a Joint Venture (i.e. all members of the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract if selected) and/or Sub-consultants (i.e. the Consultant will be responsible, including for the services of the sub-consultant).

 In case of an association, the Consultants must explain in the EOI submission (a) the rationale for forming the association and (b) the anticipated role and relevant qualifications of each member of the association and/or of each sub-consultant for carrying out the assignment, to justify the proposed inclusion of the association members and/or sub-consultants in the association. The Applicant’s attention is drawn to the following:

National consulting engineering firms shall satisfy the requirements as defined in this request for Expression of Interest and the ToR and classified as First Grade (1) in the field of Water and Wastewater as per the Government Tender Directorate (GTD) classification system;

The shortlisting criteria are as follows, in which specific experience of the Consultant relevant to the assignment will be considered of paramount importance:

  1. General Experience of the Consultant (as a firm) in providing consultant services (The firm’s core business and general experience, years in business, and overall competencies in relevance to this assignment)
  2. Specific Experience of the Consultant (as a firm) relevant to the assignment in providing similar services under contracts of comparable size (Description of similar assignments, and in similar conditions. The similar assignments will be considered only if they include a comprehensive dam safety assessment and sediment management, in the past 15 years.

 

Consultant Brochures may also be included in the EOI. To demonstrate their qualifications and experience in meeting the above shortlisting/selection criteria, Consultants are requested to submit, at a minimum, the supporting documentation listed below.  A consultant firm can only use its own qualifications and experience and not of its parent, sister or subsidiary companies or its employees. 

  1. The firm's incorporation/trade/registration documents issued by the concerned government authority of the country of the firm.
  2. The firm’s company brochures including the core areas of business; and
  3. Completed Form-1 (attached to this Request for Expression of Interest) to provide information of similar contracts. This should include the name and reference number of the contract, brief description of the scope of work, contract amount, period of the contract, name of the client and country of assignment, and role of the Consultant in the contract.  Copies of completion certificates/references of Clients of completed contracts are not required to be submitted with the EoI. In the subsequent stage at the time of submission of proposals, the Client may request the shortlisted consultants to submit such supporting completion certificates.

It is preferable to limit the EoI to a maximum of 30 pages.

The shortlist will contain a maximum of (8) Eight firms.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (REOI)

(SELECTION OF CONSULTANT FIRM/NGO)

Country: Bangladesh

Name of Project: ISO Component 05: Socio-economic Development of the Host Community and FDMN through Capacity Enhancement Project, (Credit No: IDA-7546-BD & E326-BD)

Assignment Title: Selection of Consulting Firm/NGO for Capacity Strengthening of Social workers on Elderly Care & support and Special Needs and disability Management.

Reference No.: SD-18

The Government of Bangladesh is implementing the Inclusive Services and Opportunities for Host Communities and Displaced Rohingya Population (ISO) Project with World Bank financing. The Project Development Objective is to improve access to human capital services for vulnerable host communities and displaced Rohingya populations. Component 3, implemented by the Department of Social Services (DSS) under the Ministry of Social Welfare (MoSW), supports social care, child protection, and economic empowerment interventions for the Host Communities and Forcibly Displaced Myanmar Nationals (FDMN) in Chattogram Division. Under this assignment, DSS intends to strengthen the professional capacity of its social workers to provide inclusive, rights-based and person-centred services to older persons and persons with disabilities, including assessment, care planning, case management, referral, safeguarding and community-based support.

Purpose

To strengthen the knowledge, practical competencies and professional skills of DSS social workers in delivering quality, inclusive, rights-based and person-centered services for elderly persons and persons with disabilities (PWDs). The assignment will be implemented over Fourteen (14) months.

Objectives

The consultancy/training assignment shall:

  • Enhance technical knowledge on ageing, elderly care and disability management.
  • Build skills / competencies on: (i) case management and counselling skills, (ii) assessment of functional ability and care needs, (iii) disability-inclusive social protection.
  • Enhance referral and coordination with health, rehabilitation and community services.
  • Strengthen safeguarding, protection and ethical practice.
  • Promote family and community-based care approaches.
  • Improve reporting, documentation and digital case management.
  • Build Training of Trainers (ToT) capacity within DSS.

The Department of Social Services now invites eligible consulting firms/NGOs (‘Consultants’) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

The shortlisting criteria are:

  1. Core business and years in business, including at least 10 years of experience in social development and/or institutional capacity strengthening;
  2. Experience in successfully completed or substantially completed assignments of similar nature, size and complexity, particularly assignments involving training-needs assessment, competency-based curriculum development, Training of Trainers and large-scale training related to elderly care, disability inclusion, rehabilitation, social work, case management, safeguarding or community-based support;
  3. Experience in providing capacity-development services to government or public-sector institutions in Bangladesh or comparable country contexts;
  4. Experience in competency-based curriculum development
  5. Experience in developing and conducting post training evaluation
  6. Technical and managerial capability of the firm, including its organizational structure, permanent professional capacity, quality-assurance arrangements and capacity to manage large-scale training. Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

Consultants should submit:

  1. Proof of legal establishment or registration in their country of origin;
  2. a brief firm/NGO profile, including its organizational and permanent professional capacity;
  3. Details of relevant assignments, including assignment name, client, country, implementation period, completion status, contract value, the Consultant’s role and a brief description of the services performed;
  4. Client references or evidence of satisfactory completion, where available; and
  5. The JV agreement or letter of intent to form a JV, if applicable. Detailed CVs of proposed experts are not required, as Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s ‘Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers’, Fifth Edition, September 2023 (‘Procurement Regulations’), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications and capability and should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all members of the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected. Consultants should briefly describe the respective roles of the JV members and/or subconsultants in carrying out the assignment. The qualifications and experience of subconsultants will not be considered in the evaluation of Expressions of Interest for shortlisting purposes.

A Firm will be selected in accordance with the Quality and Cost Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours, i.e. 0900 to 1600 hours. The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be downloaded from https://iso.dss.gov.bd website or can be obtained upon request from the address below either by e-mail or in person during the office hours (Local Time: 09:00 to 16:00 hours).

Expressions of interest must be delivered in a written form to the address below (in person, or by mail, or by e-mail- procurement.iso.dss.msw@gmail.com) by 19 October 2026 up to 1400 hours (UTC+ 6 hours).

The Procuring Entity (PE) reserves the right to accept or reject any or all EOIs without assigning any reason whatsoever.

Community and FDMN through Capacity Enhancement Project

Türkiye Cumhuriyeti Hükümeti, Dünya Bankas’ndan (DB), Türkiye kinci Sulama Modernizasyonu ve Su Verimlilii Projesi (TIMP-2) kapsamnda düük faizli ikraz salam olup, ikrazn bir ksm “Kahramankazan Aknc Sulamas Yenileme Projesi Yeniden Yerleim Plan le zleme ve Deerlendirme Raporlarnn Hazrlanmas Danmanlk Hizmetleri” iinde kullanlacaktr.

Bu duyuru kapsamndaki danmanlk hizmetleri genel olarak aada bahsi geçen faaliyetlerin hazrlanmas ve uygulanmasn kapsamaktadr:

  • Bir (1) adet Yeniden Yerleim Plan (YYP) hazrlanmas,
  • Arazi Piyasas Aratrma Raporunun (APAR) sunulmas,

 

  • Alt (6) aylk dönemler için toplam 8 (sekiz) adet zleme ve Deerlendirme raporu dareye sunulacaktr.

 

  • , sözlemenin imzalanmasndan itibaren alt (6) ay içinde taslak Yeniden Yerleim Plannn (YYP) sunulmas, nihai Yeniden Yerleim Plan (YYP) sunulmadan önce Arazi Piyasas Aratrma Raporunun (APAR) sunulmas ve sözlemenin imzalanmasndan itibaren sekiz (8) ay içinde nihai Yeniden Yerleim Plannn (YYP) sunulmasn gerektirir.  YYP’nin hazrlanp uygulanmasndan (arazi ediniminin balamas) balamak ve alt (6) ayda bir (1) adet olmak üzere, izleme/deerlendirme raporlarnn 48 ay boyunca hazrlanp teslimini içermektedir.

Devlet Su leri Genel Müdürlüü, yukarda tariflenen danmanlk hizmetlerini verebilecek uygun nitelikli danmanlk firmalarn ilgilerini göstermeleri için davet etmektedir. lgilenen Danmanlarn, ileri yapmaya yeterli olduunu gösteren bilgileri (broürler, yaptklar benzer ilerin tanm, benzer koullardaki tecrübeleri, uygun yeteneklere sahip personelin mevcudiyeti, vb.) sunmalar gerekmektedir.

TMP-2 kapsamnda hazrlanacak YYP için Tanmnda yer alan görevleri icra edecek yüklenicinin sahip olmas gereken asgari nitelikler aada tanmlanmtr:

  • Dünya Bankas Çevresel ve Sosyal Standart 5 (ÇSS 5) hakknda bilgi ve tecrübeye sahip olmak,
  • Kamulatrma ve Arazi Edinimi konusunda ilgili Türk mevzuatna hâkim olmak,
  • Daha önce Dünya Bankas Çevre ve Sosyal Çerçevesi ile ulusal mevzuatn gerekliliklerine uygun olarak en az bir Yeniden Yerleim Plan (YYP) ve/veya Yeniden Yerleim Eylem Plan (YYEP) hazrlam olmak,

 

Dünya Bankas Satn Alma Kurallarn kapsayan ubat 2025 tarihli 6. edisyonunda “IPF Borçlular için Satn Alma Düzenlemelerinin Dünya Bankas’nn çkar çatmas durumundaki Politikasn ortaya koyan 3.13 ve devam paragraflarn ilgili danmanlarn dikkate almas gerekmektedir.

Danmanlar, niteliklerini artrma amacyla ortak giriim kurma veya alt yüklenici çaltrma yoluyla dier firmalarla i birliine gidebilirler. Ortak Giriim (OG) durumunda, OG’nin tüm üyeleri ksa liste oluturulmas esnasnda birlikte deerlendirilecek olup ihale sonras sözleme imzalanmas durumunda hizmetlerin yerine getirilmesinden mütereken ve müteselsilen sorumlu olacak ve sözlemeyi OG adna imzalayacaklardr. lgili danmanlar “ortakln” yapsn, ortaklarn ve alt yüklenicilerin uygulamadaki görevlerini açk bir biçimde tanmlayacaktr. “... ile balantl ekilde” ve/veya ile ortaklk içinde” vb. ekilde mulak ifadeler kullanlmas ilgili firmalarn ksa listeye girememesi ile sonuçlanabilir.

Danman, Dünya Bankasnn Satn Alma Düzenlemelerinde tariflenen Danman’n Niteliine Göre Seçilmesi (CQS) yöntemine uygun olarak seçilecektir.

Konuyla ilgili daha fazla bilgiye Türkiye saatiyle 09:00 ve 17:00 arasnda içinde aada verilen adresten ulalabilir.

Danman firmalarn bavurularn Türkçe dnda bir dilde sunmak istemeleri halinde bavuruyla ilgili tüm belgeleri Türkçe tercümeleri ile birlikte sunmalar gerekmektedir.

Danman firmalarn dareye sunacaklar lgi Beyanlar son teslim tarihinden itibaren alt (6) ay süre ile geçerli saylacaktr.

REVOLUTIONARY GOVERNMENT OF ZANZIBAR

 

MINISTRY OF FINANCE AND PLANNING

 

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

 

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRM SELECTION)

 

COUNTRY:                    UNITED REPUBLIC OF TANZANIA

 

NAME OF PROJECT: BOOSTING INCLUSIVE GROWTH FOR ZANZIBAR (BIG-Z)

 

Loan No:                         IDA - 69140 –TZ

 

Assignment Title:          Consultancy Services to Support, Enhance, and Implement the Local Government Revenue Collection System (MUTM)

 

Reference No:                TZ-POFP-573107-CS-QCBS.

 

This request for expression of interest follows the General Procurement Notice for the Boosting of Inclusive Growth for Zanzibar Project (BIG-Z) that appeared in the UN Development Business online No. WB-P811333-8 of 27-08-2021.

 

The United Republic of Tanzania has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Boosting Inclusive Growth for Zanzibar Project (BIG-Z), and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

 

The Consultancy Services (“the Services”) include: conducting a comprehensive assessment of the existing Local Government Revenue Collection System (MUTM), including its functional capabilities, architecture, source code, database, data quality, security posture, performance and scalability; identifying technical, operational, legal and policy gaps and interoperability constraints; developing at least two technically feasible and costed upgrade options and a detailed implementation roadmap; and implementing the approved upgrade. The Services further include GIS enablement aligned with ZanSDI; interoperability with ZanMalipo, Zanzibar Revenue Authority systems, Ministry of Finance and Planning systems, eGAZ requirements and LARIS, as applicable; data cleansing and migration; software development and configuration; testing, User Acceptance Testing (UAT), deployment to all 12 Local Government Authorities; capacity building and Training-of-Trainers (ToT); preparation of manuals and SOPs; knowledge transfer; and post-deployment support/hypercare.

 

The duration of the services for conducting this assignment is expected to be thirty-six (36) weeks (approximately nine (9) months) from contract commencement, comprising Phase 1 (Weeks 1–16) and Phase 2 (Weeks 17–36).

 

The detailed Terms of Reference (ToR) for the assignment can be found upon request to the following email: bigzpmt@gmail.com

 

The Principal Secretary, Ministry of Finance and Planning now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the services. The shortlisting criteria are:

 

A: Core business and at least ten (10) years of experience in ICT, software development, and IT system assessment.

 

B: Relevant similar experience as specified below

 

The firm must have carried out at least one (1) assignment of a similar nature and scope involving the assessment and design of a public financial management system or municipal revenue system in a developing country.

 

The firm should demonstrate proven experience in the assessment, design, development/configuration and implementation of large-scale public-sector ICT systems, preferably financial management, municipal revenue, taxation, billing, payment, or related government information systems.

 

The consultant should demonstrate experience in system architecture, database design and administration, software development lifecycle management, performance/scalability assessment, information security, testing, User Acceptance Testing (UAT), deployment, operational handover and post-deployment support.

 

The consultant should demonstrate experience in GIS/SDI-enabled systems and geospatial interoperability, including integration of GIS workflows with enterprise applications and, where feasible, use of open-source technologies such as PostgreSQL/PostGIS, GeoServer and QGIS or equivalent technologies.

The consultant should demonstrate experience in systems interoperability and API/data exchange integration with government platforms such as e-payment gateways, revenue/tax systems, land administration systems, digital government platforms or other comparable public systems, including data migration, cleansing, reconciliation, logging and auditability.

 

Experience in capacity building and Training-of-Trainers (ToT), including development of user/admin manuals and institutional knowledge transfer, is desirable. Proven experience in Sub-Saharan Africa will be considered a significant advantage, and experience on donor-funded projects or assignments financed by international development partners will be a strong advantage.

 

C: Technical and managerial capability of the firm (Provide only the structure of the organization, general qualifications, and number of key staff). Do not provide CV of the key staff. Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

 

The attention of interested consultants is drawn to section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” Sixth Edition, February 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s Policy on conflict of interest.

Therefore, each member of JV shall independently meet the requirements of the evaluation criteria.

 

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality and Cost Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations

 

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours i.e. 07.30 am to 03.30 pm EAT excluding public holidays.

Republic of Uganda

CREDIT NO. 7779-UG and GRANT NO.: C8807

ASSIGNMENT TITLE: CONSULTANCY SERVICES TO UNDERTAKE INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION OF PROJECT RESULTS UNDER THE UGANDA LEARNING ACCELERATION PROGRAM (U-LEARN)

REFERENCE NO. MOES-ULEARN/SRVCS/2026-2027/00011

DATE OF ISSUANCE OF REOI: 23rd September 2026

The Government of the Republic of Uganda through the Ministry of Education and Sports (MoES) has received financing from the Global Partnership for Education (GPE) and the International Development Association (IDA) towards the cost of the Uganda Learning Acceleration Program (ULEARN), and intends to apply part of the proceeds for hire of an Independent Verification Agent (IVA) to conduct independent verification of results for the Uganda Learning Acceleration Program (ULEARN).

The consulting services (“the Services”) include; (i) Conducting independent verification of the achievement of all eligible Disbursement Linked Indicators (DLIs) and Disbursement Linked Results (DLRs) under ULEARN, (ii) Verification of results across the program implementation period, including document reviews, field verification, validation of reported data, assessment of compliance with agreed verification protocols, and confirmation of the achievement of results in accordance with the Financing Agreement, Programme Appraisal Document (PAD), Verification Protocol, and Project Operations Manual (POM).

The verification shall cover all implementing entities, beneficiary institutions, and geographic locations relevant to the DLIs being assessed. The IVA shall produce independent verification reports that confirm the extent to which the DLRs have been achieved. These reports shall provide a direct basis for the World Bank's assessment of DLR achievement and the corresponding disbursement recommendations under the Program.

The Independent Verification Agent (IVA) shall be engaged for the duration of the ULEARN Program implementation, expected to until run 30th June 2030 subject to satisfactory performance, continued need for the services, and availability of funding.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at the following website: www.education.go.ug or can be obtained at the address given below.

The Ministry of Education and Sports now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are:

The firm shall meet the following minimum requirements:

  1. At least ten (10) years of demonstrated experience in conducting independent verification, performance audits, Program evaluations for Government institutions.
  2. Demonstrated experience in at least three (3) assignments involving verification or evaluation of large-scale education, infrastructure, or public sector Programs within the last ten (10) years.
  3. Proven experience in verifying results under Results-Based Financing (RBF), Program-for-Results (PforR), Disbursement-Linked Indicators (DLIs), or similar performance-based financing mechanisms is highly desirable.
  4. Experience working on projects financed by the World Bank, African Development Bank, or other multilateral development partners will be an added advantage.
  5. Demonstrated capacity to deploy a multidisciplinary team comprising experts in education, engineering, procurement, financial management, environmental and social safeguards, monitoring and evaluation, Information and Technology and data management. (Please do not submit CVs and bio data of experts).
  6. Capacity to undertake nationwide field verification and quality assurance.
  7. Demonstrated experience in the use of digital data collection platforms (e.g., KoboToolbox, GEMS, ODK, Survey123, or equivalent) capable of capturing geo-tagged photographs, GPS coordinates, and date/time stamps.
  8. Experience implementing similar assignments in Uganda or the East African region or Sub-Saharan Africa will be an added advantage.
  9. Demonstrate high standards of professional integrity, independence, confidentiality, and quality assurance, and shall have no actual or perceived conflict of interest in relation to the implementation of ULEARN

Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” dated February 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. 

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, and should indicate clearly in the Expression of Interest (EOI) whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality and Cost Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours (Monday to Friday, 09:00 – 17:00 hours, except on public holidays).

The packages must be clearly marked “Expression of Interest for Consultancy Services for Independent Verification of project results under the Uganda Learning Acceleration Program (ULEARN)”

People’s Republic of China

World Bank Loan Hainan Project for Prevention, Preparedness and Response to Emerging Infectious Diseases (Global One Health Hainan Demonstration Project)

Loan No.: 9084-CN

Procurement No.: 0733-26094168

Assignment Name: Establishment and Promotion of Community Pilot Sites for Sustainable Vector Control in Tropical Areas Based on the One Health Approach

Contract No.: HN-FC-84

The Government of the People’s Republic of China has received a loan from the World Bank toward the cost of the World Bank Loan Hainan Project for Prevention, Preparedness and Response to Emerging Infectious Diseases (Global One Health Hainan Demonstration Project), and intends to apply part of the proceeds of this loan to payments for consulting services.

The consulting services (hereinafter referred to as the “Services”) mainly include the following: The consulting service period is 12 months after the contract is signed and becomes effective, and the expected commencement date of the consulting services is December 2026. The Services consist of, but are not limited to, the following 13 tasks:

  1. Preparation of the implementation plan;
  2. Selection and pre-assessment of community pilot sites;
  3. Conducting training activities;
  4. Routine mosquito prevention and control;
  5. Health education;
  6. Mosquito monitoring;
  7. Preparation of training reference materials and technical manuals;
  8. Development and maintenance of the data platform;
  9. Establishment and improvement of a multi-sectoral joint prevention and control mechanism at the community level;
  10. Development of evaluation indicators and management standards;
  11. Final evaluation of sustainable vector control communities and awarding ceremony;
  12. Provision of policy recommendations and suggestions;
  13. Data analysis and summary.

The Terms of Reference (TOR) for this consulting service are attached to this Request for Expressions of Interest.

Hainan Provincial Disease Control Bureau (hereinafter referred to as the “Client”) now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to express their interest in providing the consulting services. Interested Consultants shall provide relevant supporting documents in accordance with the following requirements. The Expression of Interest (i.e., the proposal document) shall include, at a minimum, the following:

  1. A brief introduction of the consulting firm, including its organizational structure, staffing information, etc.
  2. The Letter of Authorization, identification documents of the legal representative and the authorized representative; if the Consultant is a joint venture, the joint venture agreement shall also be provided (format to be prepared by the Consultant).
  3. The Consultant shall provide a copy of its relevant business license or Certificate of Legal Person of Public Institution.
  4. If the Consultant is a state-owned enterprise or public institution, it shall provide its Articles of Association or the approval document for its establishment, as well as the audited financial audit report and financial statements for the year 2025 (including, at a minimum, the balance sheet, cash flow statement, and income statement/profit and loss statement), or the “internal financial statements of the entity” for 2025, or the final account report approved by the competent authority, or other equivalent supporting documents. (If the Consultant is a newly established entity and is unable to provide the above-mentioned documents for 2025, it shall provide financial statements and other relevant documents since its establishment.)
  5. The Consultant shall have a good track record and reputation and shall provide a “Commitment Letter on Good Track Record and Reputation” (in a self-prepared format) affixed with the official seal of the entity.
  6. The Consultant shall have successfully completed at least two similar projects during the past five years (from January 1, 2021 to the deadline for submission of documents). Similar projects refer to consulting assignments in areas including, but not limited to, infectious disease prevention and control, public health risk assessment, establishment of various pilot programs, tropical disease research, or disease surveillance and early warning. The contract amount of each project shall be no less than RMB 1 million. The Consultant shall submit supporting documents for relevant experience, including:
    Copies of key pages of the contracts, which shall at least demonstrate key information such as the contract date, contract amount, scope of services, and signatures/seals of both parties;
    Acceptance documents demonstrating that the projects have passed evaluation and acceptance; and
    Supporting documents proving that payments have been received by the Consultant.
  7. Other documents that the Consultant considers necessary to provide (if any).

Key experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

Interested Consultants should pay attention to the provisions regarding the World Bank’s conflict of interest policy set forth in paragraphs 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (November 2020 edition).

Consulting firms may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications; however, they shall clearly indicate whether such association is in the form of a joint venture and/or subcontracting arrangement. If a joint venture arrangement is selected, all members of the joint venture shall meet the “Consultant Qualification Requirements” specified in this Request for Expressions of Interest. If the joint venture Consultant is selected, all parties of the joint venture, as well as any subcontracted Consultants, shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract.

The Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality- and Cost-Based Selection (QCBS) method specified in the Procurement Regulations.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

 

 

Country: Moldova

Name of Project: Moldova Rural Connectivity Project

Project ID: P180153

 

Assignment Title: Technical assistance for the further development of Road Asset Management System in Moldova

 

Reference No. (as per Procurement Plan): MRCP/CS/08

 

The Government of the Republic of Moldova has received financing from the World Bank (the “Bank” or the “WB”) in the form of a loan/credit toward the cost of the Moldova Rural Connectivity Project. The S.A. ”Administraia Naional a Drumurilor” (“NRA” or JSC “National Road Administration”), an implementing agency (the “Client”), intends to apply part of the proceeds of this loan/credit to eligible payments under the contract for which this Request for Expressions of Interest is issued.

NRA has developed and operates a Road Asset Management System (RAMS). However, there are still many unresolved issues that prevent the proper use of the RAMS as a key pillar for the further effective road investment and maintenance planning processes, such as: lack of integration/interoperability of sub systems; manual intensive data collection; fragmentation of roles in RAMS related data collection and utilization; non-clear future alignment with the road register; lack of the sufficient legal regulation.

NRA intends to retain a consultant to lay the strategic, technical, institutional, and legal groundwork for the modernization of NRA's Road Asset Management System, so that Moldova's national road network can be managed efficiently, cost-effectively, and in line with European standards. Specifically, consultant will be required to review business processes and recommend improvements; review of existing IT based tools, software, databases, etc. architecture and integration and recommendations for further improvement preparation; develop a future RAMS Roadmap; define the asset inventory scope and data governance framework required for the future RAMS; Policy Framework Development; develop a training program and conduct a number of in-person workshops covering mentioned above topics.

 

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be obtained following a formal request to the Client to procurement.wb@andsa.md.

 

The NRA now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Consulting Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The Consultant will be a firm or a group of firms (JVCA[1]) with previous project experience related to Construction Supervision Services.

 

The shortlisting criteria:

The following shortlisting criteria will be applied to all consulting firms (individual company or joint venture overall) that have submitted EoI:

1. Criterion: General Firm Experience

Proven general experience and verifiable track record in providing consultancy/technical assistance related to Road Asset Management Systems (RAMSs), completed within the past ten (10) years. RAMS-related consultancy/technical assistance may cover studies; strategies; policy frameworks; institutional support; or preparation of methodologies, guidelines, and standards.

Scoring:

The Consultant shall be awarded up to 20 points based on the quality and relevance of project references.

 

2. Criterion: Development or implementation of RAMS solutions

Proven specific expertise and verifiable track record in the assignments related to development or implementation of the existing RAMS solutions, deployed on local and/or national road networks with paved and unpaved roads, completed within the past ten (10) years. For the purpose of this criterion, an assignment shall be considered completed if the RAMS solution has been fully developed and/or deployed and formally accepted by the client, regardless of subsequent maintenance or update activities.

Preference will be given to projects related to the local road networks.

Scoring:

The Consultant shall be awarded up to 40 points based on the quality and relevance of project references.

 

3. Criterion: Road network data

Proven specific expertise and verifiable track record in the assignments related to road network data survey, collection, and verification to be incorporated in a developed road database, completed within the past ten (10) years.

Scoring:

The Consultant shall be awarded up to 30 points based on the quality and relevance of project references.

 

4. Criterion: Training

Proven specific expertise and verifiable track record in delivering training related to RAMS completed within the last ten (10) years, with preference given to projects related to the local road networks.

Scoring:

The Consultant shall be awarded up to 10 points based on the quality and relevance of project references.

 

As a proof, the Consultant shall prepare a table listing following information: name of the relevant assignments, year of contract’s implementation (start year, end year), information on contract value, length of road network covered, percentage carried out by Consultant in case of association of firms and short description of main activities, contracting entity/client, country/region, contact reference (name, e-mail, phone number).

The maximum score that can be awarded to the Consultant is 100 points based on the cumulative evaluation of all criteria.

 

Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

 

The submitted EOI shall not exceed 40 pages.

 

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality and Cost-Based Selection method (QCBS) set out in the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers”, February 2025, setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.15 3.16, 3.17 and 3.18 of the abovementioned World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers”, setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. 

 

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

 

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours i.e. 09:00 to 16:00 local time.

 

Expressions of Interest, in English, must be delivered to the Client to the address below, marked “Expression of Interest” for Technical assistance for the further development of Road Asset Management System in Moldova (RAMS), by e-mail or in person - one hard copy (placed in an envelope - one original and one copy and one electronic copy on memory stick), to the address mentioned below, by October 27th , 2026, at 10:00 AM, local time.

Expressions of Interest received after this time and date will not be considered. 

Consultants should be aware that distance and customs formalities may require longer than expected delivery time.

National Road Administration

Attn: Mrs. Natalia Capatina

Office 336, Bucuriei str. 12A, MD 2004

Chisinau, Republic of Moldova

E-mail: procurement.wb@andsa.md

Website: www.andsa.md

 

[1] JVCA – Joint Venture, Consortium or Association

  • Be competent in the use of standard office productivity software packages, including Microsoft Office Suite and project management software applications.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST

 

 

Country:  MOZAMBIQUE

Project:  Mphanda Nkuwa Hydroelectric Project

Agreement: Preparation Advance No. -V522-MZ.

Assignment Title: Individual Consultancy Services to Provision Hydrologist Specialist Project Advisor for providing Project Advisory to undertaking the review of the hydrological studies of the planned Mphanda Nkuwa Hydropower Project.

 

Reference: MZ-GMNK-442364-CS-INDV

 

 

 

The Government of Mozambique (GoM) hereinafter referred to as “the Borrower” have received Advance funds from International Development Association (IDA) towards the costs of the Mphanda Nkuwa Hydroelectric Project, Preparation Phase. The funds have been channeled through the Mphanda Nkuwa Hydroelectric Project Office (GMNK) as the Project Implementation Agency, and GMNK intends to apply part of the proceeds for Consulting Services for providing Project Advisory for undertaking the review of the hydrological studies of the planned Mphanda Nkuwa Hydropower Project.

 

 

The GMNK now invites eligible Individual Consultant (“Consultants”) to express their interest in providing the Services. Interested Individual Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the services. The shortlisting criteria are:

 

  1. qualification, experience and skills in providing Project advisory services for reviewing the hydrological studies of hydropower projects;
  2. a minimum of Post Graduate Degree in the relevant hydrological disciplines and must have at least 15 years of professional experience relevant to the assignment.
  3. description of similar assignments previously carried out - must have done at least two (2) similar assignments (hydrological of hydropower advisory services), and
  4. experience of working in Sub-Sahara Africa - at least one (1) of the assignments should be in Sub-Shara Africa - and other regions.

 

Evidence shall be attached as supporting documents for the Expression of Interest.

 

Objective

 

The Project is being prepared for seeking financial support of the World Bank (the “Bank”) and therefore must comply with the World Bank Safeguards Policies and Performance Standards (see the concept project information document stage at the WB website [1]).  Accordingly, the Mphanda Nkuwa Project needs to comply with the World Bank Environmental and Social Framework (ESF) – Community Health and Safety (ESS4[2]). To this effect two panel of experts (PoEs) need to be formed: (i) Panel of Experts for Dam Safety (PoE-DS); and (ii) Panel of Experts for Environmental and Social Management (PoE-ESM).

Key Responsibilities/ Scope of Reviews

 

The hydrologist will:

 

  1. Review of the hydrological studies pertaining to the long-term inflow to the reservoirs, and spillway and diversion design floods with reference to international criteria. Assess the adequacy of spillway and diversion facilities, also considering increasing hydrological variability associated with global warming. Review of soil erosion data and estimate of sediment yield into the reservoirs, estimated reservoir sedimentation, and assessment of the long-term sustainable capacity that could be maintained by implementing appropriate management strategies. Review of layouts related to sediment management of the reservoirs including sediment flushing.
  2. Review of the design of spillway and tailrace facilities including flow conditions, energy dissipation and need for hydraulic modelling.
  3. Review of the designs of the diversion works, schedule and risk factors associated with diversion during construction and with the closure of diversion works at initial reservoir filling.

 

Expected Assignment Timeline

 

The assignment is for a period of six (6) years, covering project preparation, construction, and initial reservoir filling. The initial contract will be signed for a period of 2 years, with the potential for an extension to cover the full duration of preparation and implementation. The contract will be time-based, with an annual ceiling of 20 working days, subject to extension if needed.

 

Detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be obtained at the address given below.

 

The attention of interest is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank՚s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” - September 2023 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting for the World Bank`s policy on conflict of interest.

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours 08:30 to 16:30.

 

Expression of Interest must be delivered in a written form to the address below (in person, or by e-mail) by November 24, 2025, 14:00 local time, and be clearly marked “Individual Consultancy Services to Provision the Project Hydrologist Expert for Providing Project Advisory to Undertaking Hydrological Studies Review of the Planned Mphanda Nkuwa Hydropower Project.”
